modules.doc: Asset definitions by reference: a project path, `file#entry` for one entry, `#id` for a scene block, or `id://<id>` from `assets/index.toml`. A script gets the definition table.

docs.assign_id: The id a file has, giving it one if it has none: a digest of the path and content, written to `assets/index.toml` and, for an asset document, as its top-level `id`. Reference it as `id://<id>` afterwards.
docs.directory: The project-relative directory files of an asset type belong in; empty when the type is unknown or declared none.
docs.duplicate: A private copy of a definition, read past the cache, so editing it disturbs no other holder of that reference.
docs.exists: Whether a reference resolves to a definition that is really there; false rather than an error when it does not.
docs.id: The id `assets/index.toml` gives a file, or nil when it has none.
docs.invalidate: Declare everything derived from project files stale (a shader a material links, say) so it is rebuilt from disk; for a file the watcher does not cover.
docs.load: The definition table behind a reference, from the cache; an error when the reference resolves to nothing.
docs.path: The path an `id://` reference resolves to in the running project; a path comes back as itself, and an unknown id is an error naming the index.
docs.reload: Forget a reference so the next load re-reads its file, along with every entry cut from that same file.
docs.rename: Move a file or directory and rewrite every reference to it in the project's `.toml` files, comments kept; answers the files rewritten. Paths as `fs.*` takes them, so an editor refactors the game it has open by absolute path. Script sources are not rewritten: a path in a `.rn` is the script's own value, and `id://` is the reference that survives a move.
docs.save: Write a definition table to the project-relative file a reference names; an error unless it names a whole file.

modules.doc: Sound playback: `play` starts a node's `sound` component and returns a handle that `stop_playback`, `set_volume_linear`, `set_pitch_scale` and `is_playing` take; `seek` and `skip` move it. `play_cue` plays a sound named in `audio/cues.toml`, from a `position` heard from the `listener` when given one. A node's `sound` announces `finished` (`EVENT_FINISHED`) with the handle when it plays out. `devices` lists the outputs `[audio] device` can name.

docs.bus_limit: One bus's limiter as `[audio.buses]` declares it: `limit`, `limit_threshold_db`, `limit_knee_db`, `limit_attack_time` and `limit_release_time`. Nil for a bus with none.
docs.bus_volume_linear: One bus's own gain, without its parents'.
docs.buses: Every audio bus, declared in `[audio.buses]` or made by setting a volume, in name order.
docs.cues: Every sound named in `audio/cues.toml`, in name order.
docs.device_ready: Whether an output device is open. False on a page until the first gesture, and false for good with no sound card; playing before then hands out handles that make no sound.
docs.devices: Every output device's name, as `[audio] device` takes it. Empty when the platform lists none.
docs.distance_gain: The gain the distance to the listener is costing a positional handle right now: 1 up close, 0 out of range.
docs.emitter_position: Where a handle played with a `position` is; nil for a flat or unknown one.
docs.is_playing: Whether a handle's sound is still going: false once it plays out or is stopped, on the same tick with or without an output device.
docs.listener_position: Where the ears are: the current `listener` node's world position, or what `set_listener_position` last put there.
docs.pan: Where a positional handle sits between the speakers: -1 hard left, 0 centred, 1 hard right.
docs.play: Start the node's own `sound` from the top, replacing what it had going, and return the new handle.
docs.play_cue: Play a named sound: the next of its variations in turn, at its own volume and pitch, through its own bus. A `position` in the options table places it. Nil for a name nothing declared.
docs.seek: Jump the node's sound to `seconds` into the file it is playing; `playback_time` reads it back. A node with nothing playing is left alone.
docs.set_bus_volume_linear: Set one bus's gain and re-apply it to everything already playing on it: which is what a volume slider is.
docs.set_emitter_position: Move what a handle plays from, so a sound follows something the script is driving; the frame takes its doppler from how far it moved.
docs.set_listener_position: Put the ears at a point by hand, for a game whose view is not a node; a `listener` node in the scene takes it back on the next frame.
docs.set_pitch_scale: Set a playing handle's speed multiplier, which carries its pitch with it.
docs.set_volume_linear: Set a playing handle's linear gain, where 1 is the file's own level.
docs.skip: Move the node's sound on to the next file in its `queue`. Past the last one it has played out, and the node announces `finished`.
docs.stop: Silence what the node's `sound` started, over its `fade_out_time`; a node carrying none is left alone.
docs.stop_all: Silence everything at once and clear the playback every `sound` component was holding.
docs.stop_playback: Silence the sound a handle names, over the `fade_out_time` its `sound` had; a finished, stopped or unknown handle is left alone.

modules.doc: The page a browser build runs in; off the web every query answers nil. A parent-frame message reaches `on_browser_event` on every node that called `listen`.

docs.hardware_concurrency: How many threads the browser reports, or nil off the web.
docs.listen: Have the node's `on_browser_event(payload)`, or the `on_event` method the options name, called for every message the parent frame posts.
docs.location: The page's URL, or nil off the web.
docs.messages: Every message the parent frame posted this tick, for a script that would rather ask than declare a method.
docs.post_message: Post a value to the page that embeds this one. False off the web, and false while a recording plays.
docs.stop_listening: Stop the node hearing the parent frame's messages. Not an error when it never listened.
docs.user_agent: The browser's user agent string, or nil off the web.
docs.visible: Whether the tab is in front of the player; true off the web.

modules.doc: Breakpoints, pausing a script and resuming it. The editor's Debugger dock and the Debug Adapter Protocol server drive the same machinery.

docs.break_on_error: Whether a script that throws stops rather than being logged.
docs.breakpoints: The lines one file's breakpoints landed on.
docs.request_break: Ask to stop at the next line any script runs; nothing is stopped yet when it returns.
docs.resume: Let the stopped script go on, in the given step mode (`CONTINUE`, `STEP_OVER`, `STEP_INTO`, `STEP_OUT`).
docs.scope: The node whose subtree a pause holds still, or nil when a pause stops the whole tree.
docs.set_break_on_error: Stop where a script throws instead of logging it and moving on; off by default.
docs.set_breakpoints: Replace one file's breakpoints with the given lines, returning the lines they landed on.
docs.set_scope: Limit the pause to one node's subtree, so an editor keeps running while the game stops; nil means the whole tree.
docs.stop_location: Where a script is stopped (node, path, line, reason and frames, innermost first) or nil while none is.

modules.doc: Bytes to base64 text and back.

docs.base64: Bytes, or a string's UTF-8, as standard base64 with padding.
docs.from_base64: The bytes a base64 string encodes; an error for text that is not base64.

modules.name: encoding

modules.doc: The running app: its clock, command-line `args`, `user_data_dir`, loaded `plugins` and `quit`.

docs.args: The command-line arguments the app was started with, empty when it was given none.
docs.dark_mode: Whether the system is in dark mode this tick; every script's `on_dark_mode_changed(bool)` is called when it changes. False where nothing says.
docs.delta: Seconds the frame in progress covers, the same number a system is handed.
docs.device_id: One id per install, made on first use and kept in the user directory: what a device login sends. Recorded with the session.
docs.environment: An environment variable's value, nil when it is unset. Nil on the web, which has none. Outside the simulation, like `args`: a replay does not record it.
docs.focused: Whether the window is in front of the player this tick; every script's `on_focused_changed(bool)` is called when it changes. True with no window.
docs.function_costs: What each function has cost since `set_script_profiling(true)`, dearest first: a list of `{ function, calls, instructions }`, a function's own instructions without its callees'. A `draw` callback and a closure a native call runs are in it.
docs.has_plugin: Whether one plugin loaded, so a game shipped without `http` can say so rather than call into a module that is not there.
docs.open_url: Open an http, https or mailto URL in whatever the player browses with: an opener on a desktop, a new tab on the web. Not on iOS or Android yet, where it reports that it has no opener. An effect on the world outside the game: never recorded, and it does nothing while a recording plays.
docs.plugin_version: The version of one loaded plugin, or nil when it did not load.
docs.plugins: Every plugin this build loaded, named, in load order.
docs.quit: Ask the app to shut down; the frame in flight still finishes, and the process exits with `code`, 0 when left out.
docs.reload_script: Recompile one script by its project-relative key, for a tool editing files outside the watched root.
docs.reveal: Show a file or directory in the system file manager, selected where the platform can. Desktops only: neither a browser tab nor a phone has a file manager to ask. Never recorded, like `open_url`.
docs.script_costs: What each script has cost since `set_script_profiling(true)`, dearest first: a list of `{ path, calls, instructions }`. Instructions, not seconds, so the number is the same on every machine.
docs.set_paused: Pause or resume the game. Every node whose `process` mode is `pausable` stops ticking, physics holds both worlds, and the frame loop keeps drawing; an `always` subtree is what a pause menu runs in. Every script's `on_paused_changed(bool)` follows, the ones the pause just stopped included.
docs.set_script_profiling: Start or stop counting what each script costs. Turning it on clears the tally.
docs.set_time_scale: Multiply wall-clock time before the simulation is owed it: 0.5 is slow motion, 2.0 fast forward, each still whole fixed steps. Zero stops time without stopping a single node. A replay and a networked session drive by tick and ignore it.
docs.target: Where this runs: `{ os, web, mobile, touchscreen, editor, dev }`, `dev` being a run from the sources rather than an exported pack. Recorded in a session's header, so a replay on another machine answers as the original did.
docs.tick: Which frame this is, counted whole: what simulation code branches on instead of `time`.
docs.tick_hz: How many fixed steps a second this run takes, from `[time] tick_hz`. 60 unless the project says otherwise.
docs.time: Seconds of engine time since the app started, accumulated as a float.
docs.time_scale: What time is being multiplied by; 1.0 is real time.
docs.timings: What the last frame cost, in seconds: `{ frame, fixed_steps, stages, spans }`. Presentation only: branching a `fixed_update` on wall time desyncs, and nothing records it.
docs.unix_time: The wall clock at the top of this tick, in seconds since 1970. Read once per frame and recorded, so a replay sees the time the recording saw.
docs.user_data_directory: A writable per-user directory for saves and settings, created on first call and named after the project.
docs.user_data_directory_of: The user data directory a project of that name has, not created: where a tool finds another game's saves and logs.

modules.name: engine

modules.doc: Named events between scripts. A node listens for a name and hears it as its `on_<name>` method; `node.emit` and `events.emit` send one.

docs.emit: Queue an event from no particular node, delivered at the top of the next frame's update to whoever listens for the name from anyone.
docs.emitted: The payloads delivered under this name this frame whoever emitted them, in emission order; empty when none were.
docs.emitted_from: The payloads delivered under this name this frame from that node, in emission order; empty when none were.
docs.listen: Hear an event on this node, as its script's `on_<name>(payload)`. Pass the node whose events to hear, or leave it out for every emitter. Listening twice is once.
docs.next: A token for `task.wait` that wakes, with the payload, the next time the name is delivered from that node or, left out, from anyone: `let payload = task::wait(events::next("finished", door)).await;`, a GDScript `await door.finished`.
docs.stop_listening: Stop hearing an event on this node, `from` being the emitter it listened with. Not an error when it never listened.

modules.name: events

modules.doc: Exports the project being edited. `targets` lists what this install can build; `start` runs one off the frame and reports to `on_export_event`.

docs.listen: Have the node's `on_export_event(event)`, or the `on_event` method the options name, called as each export starts, finishes or fails.
docs.output: Where an export for this target will be written, as the project's `[export] output` decides.
docs.preview: What one file becomes in a target's pack, as the Import tab shows it: `{ source, before, after, width, height, drawn_width, drawn_height, gpu_bytes }`, where `source` is the file or the variant that ships and `drawn_*` is zero unless a smaller copy does. Nil when the file does not ship there. An empty target is this machine's own.
docs.running_count: How many exports are in flight.
docs.start: Export the edited project for one target, on a thread. `download` allows fetching a missing template, `sign` names an identity, `output` overrides where it lands. Answers false while a recording plays.
docs.targets: Every target, each `{ name, runtime, bundle, installed, fetchable, note }`: the runtime the project's `[export] runtime` puts it on, whether that is already here, whether a missing one could be fetched, and what a signed build of it would also need.

modules.name: export

modules.doc: Files on disk, project-relative unless the path is absolute. A packed build's contents are reached through `assets` and `scene.source`.

docs.copy: Copy a file byte for byte, creating the destination's parent first. What `read` and `write` cannot do for an image or a model.
docs.create_directory: Create a project-relative directory and every parent it needs.
docs.exists: Whether a project-relative path has anything at it, file or directory.
docs.list: A directory's entries as `{ name, is_dir }`, sorted, dotfiles skipped; empty for a directory that is not there.
docs.modified_time: When a file last changed, in seconds since the Unix epoch; nil for one that is not there.
docs.read: A whole file as text, project-relative unless absolute; nil when it cannot be read.
docs.remove: Delete a project-relative file, or a directory and everything under it; false when there was nothing there.
docs.rename: Move a project-relative file or directory, creating the destination's parent first.
docs.write: Write text to a project-relative file, creating the directory it goes in.

modules.name: fs

modules.doc: The Gamend backend: session, REST API and realtime socket. Each call returns an id to await; the result also reaches the node's `on_gamend_event` (or `on_event`) as a map whose `kind` is an `EVENT_*` constant.

docs.activity: The last calls and socket messages, newest first, as `{ seq, request, kind, what, status, ms, args, reply }`, `seq` counting every row ever kept; `ms` is nil while a call waits, and only the newest fifty keep `args` and `reply`. An observer: never simulate from it.
docs.call_hook: Call a server plugin's function over the socket; the reply's `response` holds `data` or `error`.
docs.clear_activity: Forget the calls and messages `activity` holds.
docs.close: Shut the socket down; false when the connection was already gone.
docs.configure: Point the plugin at a server and answer its url; with none, the one `[gamend]` names for this run (see `target`). Every other call errors until this one runs.
docs.connect: Open the realtime socket and return the id `join`, `push`, `leave`, `call_hook` and `close` take, which `task.wait` resumes on with the `open` or `error` event. A dropped connection comes back on its own: the handler hears `reconnecting` before each try, then `reopened` once its topics are joined again, or `error` when it gives up.
docs.connection: The configured `url`, who is signed in (`user_id`, `username`), and each socket as `{ socket, open, topics, reason }`.
docs.interrupt: Cut the connection as a network failure would, to try a game's reconnect path: the socket reports `reconnecting`, then `reopened`. False when it is already gone.
docs.join: Subscribe the socket to a topic and return the id the server's `reply` answers.
docs.leave: Unsubscribe the socket from a topic, returning the id the `reply` answers.
docs.login: Open a session from a `device_id`, or an `email` and `password`, and return the id its `login` result answers.
docs.push: Send an event and its payload to a topic on the socket, returning the id the `reply` answers.
docs.register: Make an account from an `email` and a `password` (and a `username`, generated when left out) and open its session, as `login` does; its result is a `login` one. The server mails the address its confirmation link.
docs.reply: What a call answered, as its event map, once it has; nil while it waits. The newest sixty-four are kept, so a drawing loop can issue a call and read it back on a later frame.
docs.rest: Call a path on the configured server over HTTP; the result carries the `status` and the decoded `body`.
docs.restore: Sign in from a session a previous run kept, as `session` answers it, without asking the server; nil signs out here. False when there is no server to sign in to, or the map carries no `access_token`.
docs.run_id: This run's id: every call sends it as `x-gamend-session` and the socket as `client_session`, so the server files a run's lines together. The log shipper names its run with it.
docs.server: The server a `configure()` with no URL uses: `{ name, url, production, local, plugin }` from `[gamend]`, `name` being `production` or `local`.
docs.session: The signed-in session as `{ user_id, username, display_name, access_token, refresh_token, expires_in, expires_at }`, `expires_at` read from the token itself; nil when nobody is signed in.

modules.name: gamend

modules.doc: Polygons on the plane as lists of `[x, y]` points in outline order: triangulation, booleans, hulls and containment. Every answer is identical on every platform.

docs.area: The polygon's area, always positive whatever its winding.
docs.contains: Whether a point lies inside the polygon; a point on an edge counts as inside.
docs.convex_decomposition: The polygon cut into convex pieces that overlap across their seams, so nothing wedges into one; `overlap` from 0 to 1 says how far each piece grows, 0.9 by default.
docs.convex_hull: The smallest convex polygon around the points, counter-clockwise.
docs.difference: Everything inside the first polygon and outside the second, shaped and tuned as `union` is.
docs.intersection: Everything inside both polygons, shaped and tuned as `union` is.
docs.is_clockwise: Whether the points run clockwise, with y up.
docs.reverse_difference: Everything inside the second polygon and outside the first, shaped and tuned as `union` is.
docs.segments_intersect: Where two segments cross, or nil when they do not; touching at an endpoint counts.
docs.symmetric_difference: Everything inside exactly one of the two polygons, shaped and tuned as `union` is.
docs.triangulate: The polygon cut into triangles, as `[i, j, k]` triples indexing its points, counter-clockwise; either winding is accepted.
docs.union: Everything inside either polygon: a list of shapes, each a list of paths whose first is the outline and the rest holes. `opts` takes `fill_rule` (`even_odd`, `non_zero`, `positive`, `negative`; `even_odd` unless given), `min_area`, `keep_collinear` and `clean_result`, as `boolean2d` does.

modules.name: geometry2d

modules.doc: Mesh operations: hulls, convex decomposition, voxelisation, cutting and boolean intersection. A mesh is an asset name or a table of `points` and `indices`.

docs.convex_decomposition: The mesh cut into convex pieces, each one a mesh: the only way to collide a concave shape dynamically.
docs.convex_hull: The tightest convex shape containing every point: what a dynamic collider wants when the model is concave.
docs.intersect: The mesh both meshes have in common, or nothing when they do not overlap.
docs.pieces: The mesh's separate parts, one mesh each: what a model that was already broken is made of.
docs.split: Cut the mesh with a plane, returning the two halves: `#{ point = [..], normal = [..] }`.
docs.voxelize: The mesh as a voxel grid (`#{ size, cells }`, ready to be a `voxels` asset) so a model can become destructible terrain.

modules.name: geometry3d

modules.doc: SHA-256 content hashes of files and strings.

docs.sha256: The SHA-256 of a file as lowercase hex, read through the project's file roots; an absolute path is read as given.
docs.sha256_text: The SHA-256 of a string as lowercase hex.

modules.name: hash

modules.doc: HTTP requests off the frame: `method`, `headers`, `body`, `timeout_seconds` and `save_to` options. The reply reaches `on_response` as a map whose `kind` is `response`, with `status`, `headers` and `body`, or `error`; `save_to` downloads report to `on_progress` with `kind` `progress`, and a body over 256 KB going out with `kind` `upload`, natively; a browser's fetch does not report one. Each kind is an `EVENT_*` constant.

docs.cancel: Stop waiting on a request: its reply is dropped, a download stops writing, and the handler and any await hear `kind` `cancelled` next frame. False when it had already finished.
docs.request: Start an HTTP request and return the id its reply carries, to await or to match inside the handler. With `save_to` the body is written under the user directory and the reply says where in `path`.

modules.name: http

modules.doc: Imports a `.glb` or `.gltf` model, an `.aseprite` sprite, or a `.tmx` or `.ldtk` level into the project being edited, with the importers `balaur import` runs.

docs.cancel: Stop the imports in flight at the end of the file each is writing. What they had written stays where it landed; each reports `cancelled` with the count it reached.
docs.choose: Ask the reader for a file and import what they pick, reporting as `start` does. On a desktop that is the OS dialog; in a tab it is the page's own chooser, which takes several files at once so a `.gltf` can be picked with the images it names. Answers whether the asking began.
docs.file: Import one file into the edited project, in one call. Answers `{ files, scene, note }`: the project-relative paths written, the scene to instantiate when there is one, and a line for the log. Answers `{ error }` when the import failed. A whole project is the work of seconds, so an editor keeping its frame wants `start`.
docs.handles: Whether an importer claims this file, by extension.
docs.listen: Have the node's `on_import_event(event)`, or the `on_event` method the options name, called as an import starts, writes each file, finishes or fails.
docs.running_count: How many imports are in flight.
docs.start: Import one file into the edited project, or into `project` when one is named, a few files per frame, reporting each to whatever `listen` named. Answers false while a recording plays. A model and a sprite are read first and then written a slice at a time, and a Godot project is walked a few files at a time; a level walks its own folder and takes one long slice, which says so in `files`.

modules.name: import

modules.doc: One frame of input: keyboard, mouse, touch screen and gamepads, plus what went down or came up this frame. A headless run answers every query neutrally.

docs.action_down: Whether the action is held down now.
docs.action_just_pressed: Whether the action went down this frame.
docs.action_just_released: Whether the action came up this frame.
docs.action_value: How far the action is pushed, -1 to 1; a key answers 0 or 1, a stick or `keys:KeyA,KeyD` the whole range.
docs.actions: Every action `[input.actions]` declares, so a rebinding screen can list them.
docs.bind: Rebind the action to one binding or a list of them, replacing what it had and saving to the user data directory.
docs.bindings: What the action is bound to now, whether from the project or from the player's own rebinding.
docs.composing: The text an input method is still composing, for a field to show under its caret; empty once it commits into `typed`, and always empty without an input method.
docs.dropped_files: The absolute paths of files dropped onto the window this frame, in drop order; desktop only.
docs.feed_action: Put a value into an action for one frame without a binding, the way a `touch_button` does; the furthest from rest wins where something else feeds the same action. Takes effect on the next tick, since actions derive at the top of one.
docs.feed_gamepad: Report a pad as if a backend had, from next frame: `buttons` and `axes` maps of name to value, `power` as `gamepad_power` reads it, `gyro`, `acceleration`, `touches`, and the identity keys `name`, `os_name`, `guid`, `vendor`, `product`, `mapping` and `rumble`. A pad fed anything connects; `connected: false` unplugs it.
docs.feed_key: Press or release a `KEY_*` key as if the window had reported it: next frame's edge, and the state until the opposite feed.
docs.feed_mouse: Move the cursor to a window-pixel position as if the window had reported it, from next frame; the delta accumulates for that frame.
docs.feed_mouse_button: Press or release a `MOUSE_BUTTON_*` button as if the window had reported it, from next frame.
docs.feed_scroll: Turn the wheel as if the window had reported it, from next frame; adds to that frame's `scroll_delta`.
docs.feed_touch: Put a finger on the screen as if the window had reported it: `phase` is `start`, `move`, `end` or `cancel`, and the position is in the same pixels as `mouse_position`.
docs.gamepad_acceleration: The pad's acceleration in g, gravity included, so a pad at rest reads 1 on one axis. Read from PlayStation pads on desktop; zero for a pad with no accelerometer.
docs.gamepad_axis: How far the pad's `GAMEPAD_AXIS_*` stick or trigger is pushed: a stick -1 to 1 with up and right positive, a trigger 0 to 1, after `[input] gamepad_deadzone`; zero at rest and for an absent pad.
docs.gamepad_can_rumble: Whether the pad has motors to rumble; false for a pad that is not connected.
docs.gamepad_down: Whether the pad's `GAMEPAD_BUTTON_*` button is held down: pressed past `[input] gamepad_press`, and not yet back under `gamepad_release`.
docs.gamepad_gyro: How fast the pad is turning, in radians per second about each axis. Read from PlayStation pads on desktop; zero for a pad with no gyroscope.
docs.gamepad_info: Who the pad is: `{ os_name, guid, vendor, product, mapping }`, with `guid` SDL's 32 hex digits and `mapping` either `sdl` or `driver`. Empty for an absent pad.
docs.gamepad_just_pressed: Whether the pad's `GAMEPAD_BUTTON_*` button went down this frame; a press and a release between two frames are both seen.
docs.gamepad_just_released: Whether the pad's `GAMEPAD_BUTTON_*` button came up this frame; true for that one frame only.
docs.gamepad_name: The pad's name: its mapping's when one matched, else the platform's. Empty when no pad has that id.
docs.gamepad_power: The pad's power, `{ state, level }`: a `GAMEPAD_POWER_*` state and a charge from 0 to 1, or -1 when not known. Read whenever the pad sends anything.
docs.gamepad_pressure: How far the pad's `GAMEPAD_BUTTON_*` button is pressed, 0 to 1, before any deadzone: a digital button reads 0 or 1, a trigger or a pressure-sensitive button anything between.
docs.gamepad_repeated: True the frame the pad's `GAMEPAD_BUTTON_*` button goes down, then every `[input] gamepad_repeat_interval_seconds` once it has been held for `gamepad_repeat_delay_seconds`: for stepping through a menu.
docs.gamepad_rumble: Rumble the pad. Options: `strong` and `weak`, the two motors at 0..1; `duration` in seconds; `delay` before it starts; `pulse` and `gap` to beat on and off; `attack`, `attack_level`, `fade` and `fade_level` to shape each pulse; `position` with `min_distance`, `max_distance`, `falloff` (`inverse`, `linear` or `exponential`) and `rolloff` to weaken it with distance from `gamepad_set_listener`. Returns whether the pad can rumble; a second rumble replaces the first.
docs.gamepad_set_listener: Where the pad's player is, for a rumble given a `position`; until set, a placed rumble plays at full strength.
docs.gamepad_stop_rumble: Silence the pad now, without the `on_gamepad_rumble_finished` a rumble's natural end sends.
docs.gamepad_touches: Every finger on the pad's touchpad as `{ id, x, y }`, oldest first, with x and y running 0 to 1 across the surface. Read from PlayStation pads on desktop; empty for a pad with no touchpad.
docs.gamepads: The ids of every connected pad: player slots from 0. A pad takes the lowest free slot last held by the same model, else the lowest free slot, and keeps it while connected.
docs.key_down: Whether the `KEY_*` key is held down right now, however many frames it has been down. `KEY_SHIFT`, `KEY_CONTROL`, `KEY_ALT` and `KEY_META` answer for either side.
docs.key_just_pressed: Whether the `KEY_*` key went down this frame; true for that one frame only.
docs.key_just_released: Whether the `KEY_*` key came up this frame; true for that one frame only.
docs.keyboard_height: How much of the window the on-screen keyboard covers, in pixels from the bottom: what a form moves up by. Zero with no keyboard up, and always zero on a desktop.
docs.long_press: Where a finger has been held still past `long_press_seconds`, as `{ x, y }`. Reported once per finger, on the frame the hold passes; empty otherwise.
docs.mouse_delta: How far the cursor moved this frame, in pixels; movement, not a position.
docs.mouse_down: Whether the `MOUSE_BUTTON_*` button is held down right now, however many frames it has been down.
docs.mouse_just_pressed: Whether the `MOUSE_BUTTON_*` button went down this frame; true for that one frame only.
docs.mouse_just_released: Whether the `MOUSE_BUTTON_*` button came up this frame; true for that one frame only.
docs.mouse_position: The cursor's position in window pixels, with (0, 0) at the top-left corner.
docs.pan: Two or more fingers moving together as `{ x, y }`, the average movement since last frame in the same pixels as `mouse_position`. Zero with fewer than two down.
docs.pinch: Two fingers moving apart or together as `{ scale, x, y }`: `scale` above 1 is apart, measured against last frame, and `x`/`y` are the point between them. Empty with fewer than two fingers down.
docs.reset_bindings: Drop every saved rebinding and go back to what the project declared.
docs.scroll_delta: How far the wheel turned this frame, as an (x, y) pair; zero when it did not turn.
docs.swipe: A finger that travelled far enough before it lifted, as `{ x, y, speed }`: a unit direction and pixels per second. Reported on the frame it lifted and never again; empty otherwise.
docs.touches: Every finger on the screen as `{ id, x, y }`, oldest first, in the same pixels as `mouse_position`.
docs.touches_just_ended: The ids of the fingers that lifted or were cancelled this frame.
docs.touches_just_started: The ids of the fingers that touched down this frame.
docs.typed: The characters typed this frame, in order: what a text field appends, where `key_just_pressed` says which key went down.
docs.vibrate: Buzz the device for that many seconds: a phone's motor, or a page's `navigator.vibrate`. Nothing on a desktop, and never recorded, like rumble.

modules.name: input

modules.doc: JSON text to and from script values. Its `null` keeps nil through a round trip.

docs.encode: A value written back out as JSON text; NaN, infinity, a node or a callback has no JSON form and is an error.
docs.parse: The value a JSON document describes; an error on text that does not parse.

modules.name: json

modules.doc: The `info`, `warn` and `error` levels a script writes at, and the buffer behind them. Lines go through the engine's own `tracing` stream.

docs.clear: Empty the buffer, so a console reading it starts again from nothing.
docs.error: Write a line at error level, tagged as coming from a script.
docs.file: The file this run's log is written to, or nil when it keeps none. `[log] file` turns it off and `[log] keep` says how many past runs stay beside it.
docs.info: Write a line at info level, tagged as coming from a script.
docs.recent: The last n buffered entries, 100 by default, each `{ seq, time, level, tag, message, fields }`.
docs.since: What was logged after `cursor` (a `seq`, 0 for all the buffer holds), as `{ entries, cursor, missed }`: pass `cursor` back next time, and `missed` counts lines the buffer dropped before they were read.
docs.warn: Write a line at warning level, tagged as coming from a script.

modules.name: log

modules.doc: Deterministic float maths backed by pure-Rust `libm`: the same inputs give the same bits on every platform.

docs.abs: The magnitude, with the sign dropped.
docs.acos: The angle in radians whose cosine is the argument, from 0 to PI; NaN outside -1..1.
docs.asin: The angle in radians whose sine is the argument, from -PI/2 to PI/2; NaN outside -1..1.
docs.atan: The angle in radians whose tangent is the argument; with two arguments, the y-then-x form instead.
docs.atan2: The angle in radians from the positive x axis to the point, taking y first and x second.
docs.ceil: The smallest whole number at or above the argument, still a float.
docs.clamp: The first argument held inside the range given by the second (low) and third (high).
docs.cos: The cosine of an angle in radians.
docs.exp: e raised to the given power.
docs.floor: The largest whole number at or below the argument, still a float.
docs.log: The natural logarithm, or the logarithm in the base given as a second argument.
docs.log10: The base-10 logarithm; -INF at zero and NaN below it.
docs.pow: The first argument raised to the power of the second.
docs.round: The nearest whole number, with halfway cases going away from zero.
docs.sin: The sine of an angle in radians.
docs.sqrt: The square root; NaN for a negative argument.
docs.tan: The tangent of an angle in radians.

modules.name: math

modules.doc: Host, join and play a rollback match. Set this machine's input with `set_input` and read every slot's with `rollback.input(slot)`; events reach every script's `on_multiplayer_event` as a map with a `kind`.

docs.add_bot: On a host, a slot its own script plays with `set_input_for`; answers the slot, or nil when the lobby is full.
docs.host: Listen and take slot 0; answers `{ url, cert_hash, transport }`, what a joiner needs. Options over `[multiplayer]`: `transport`, `address`, `players`, `scene`, `depth`, `timeout_seconds`, `name`, `token`.
docs.join: Dial a host at a `ws://` or `https://` url; `connected` or `failed` follows. Options: `cert_hash` for a self-signed host, `name`, `token`, `timeout_seconds`.
docs.leave: Say goodbye and go idle; a host leaving ends the match for everyone.
docs.local_player: This machine's own slot, or nil before it has one.
docs.players: Every slot as `{ slot, name, bot, local, status }`, `status` as of the tick being simulated.
docs.set_input: What this machine's player does on the next tick, until set again; ignored while a tick re-runs.
docs.set_input_for: The same for a bot slot this machine plays.
docs.settled_tick: The tick before which nothing can be rolled back any more.
docs.start: On a host, start with whoever is in rather than waiting for `players`; false when there is no lobby to start.
docs.stats: `{ rtt_ms, loss, bytes_in, bytes_out }` for the link a slot is reached over; nil for this machine's own. An observer: never simulate from it.
docs.tick: The match tick being simulated; what a match branches on instead of `engine.tick`.

modules.name: multiplayer

modules.doc: What every node has: name, path, transform, children, components and script. Each function takes the node first; scripts call it as a method, `this.node.get_node("Arm")`.

docs.add_child: Create a named child node under this one and return it.
docs.add_tag: File the node under a name; `scene.tagged` finds it from then on.
docs.attach_script: Attach the script at a path, with an optional table overriding what the script exports.
docs.call: Call a method on the node's script and return what it gives back; nil when there is no such script or method.
docs.call_async: Call a method that may suspend, and get a token `task.wait` resumes with its result once it returns: `task::wait(door.call_async("open")).await`, a GDScript `await door.open()`.
docs.children: The node's direct children, an empty list when it has none.
docs.component_names: The names of every component on the node.
docs.descendants: Every node under this one, in tree order, the node itself excluded.
docs.detach_script: Drop the script instance on this node, so no further lifecycle call reaches it; the node and its components stay.
docs.effective_material: The material the node draws with: its own, or the nearest ancestor's. Empty is the built-in one.
docs.effective_tint: What the renderer multiplies by: this node's tint with every ancestor's folded in.
docs.effective_z_index: The layer the node actually draws on, with every ancestor's added in.
docs.emit: Emit an event from this node, delivered at the top of the next frame to whoever subscribed to `name` on this node, and to whoever subscribed to `name` from anyone. `call` is the twin that reaches one known script, now.
docs.get_component: The named component's properties as a table, nil when the node does not carry it. With a key, that one property rather than the table, which is what a caller reading a single value should ask for.
docs.get_node: The node at an `A/B/C` path relative to this one, `..` climbing to the parent and a leading `/` starting from the root; nil when nothing matches.
docs.global_position: The node's position in world space, as of the last transform sync.
docs.global_rotation_euler: The node's world rotation as euler angles in radians, as of the last transform sync.
docs.global_scale: The node's scale in world space, as of the last transform sync.
docs.has_component: Whether the node carries the named component.
docs.has_method: Whether the node's script declares this method, so a caller can tell "no handler" from "a handler that answered nothing".
docs.has_tag: Whether the node is filed under a name.
docs.interpolate: Whether the node is drawn between fixed steps.
docs.is_valid: Whether the node is still in the world; false rather than an error when the value is not a node.
docs.material: The `material` asset the node names itself, empty when it takes its parent's.
docs.name: The node's own name, empty when it carries none.
docs.parent: The node's parent, nil at the root.
docs.patch_component: Change the properties the table names and leave the rest of the component where they were. On a node without the component this adds it, the schema defaults being what it currently holds.
docs.path: The node's slash-separated path, built by climbing parents from the node up to the root.
docs.process: When this node ticks: "inherit", "pausable", "when_paused", "always" or "disabled". "inherit" is the default and takes the nearest ancestor's answer.
docs.queue_free: Destroy the node and its subtree at the end of the frame.
docs.remove_component: Take the named component off the node.
docs.remove_tag: Take a name off the node; a name it never had is left alone.
docs.reset_interpolation: Throw away the poses the node was blending and start again from where it is, so a teleport does not streak across the level. `physics3d.teleport` and `physics2d.teleport` call it for you.
docs.script_field: A member the node's script instance holds, read by another script: GDScript's `node.speed`. Nil for no script or no such member.
docs.script_path: The path of the script attached to the node, nil when it has none.
docs.set_component: Give the node the named component, built from the given table over the component's schema defaults. Every property the table leaves out goes back to its default; `patch_component` is the one that changes a property and leaves the rest.
docs.set_interpolate: Draw the node between fixed steps, or stop. Needs `[time] interpolate` on; a body and a script with `fixed_update` ask for it on their own.
docs.set_material: Draw the node and every descendant naming none with a `material` asset; empty goes back to the parent's.
docs.set_name: Rename the node, doing nothing when it carries no name.
docs.set_parent: Move the node under another, keeping where it is in the world; an error for a cycle or a dead parent.
docs.set_process: Set when the node and its subtree tick. "always" runs through a pause, which is what a pause menu is; "when_paused" runs only while paused; "disabled" never runs; "inherit" goes back to the parent's. Physics is one world and is held whole by a pause whatever this says.
docs.set_sibling_index: Move the node to that place among its siblings, clamped to the end. Order is draw order in a `row` or a `column`, and tree order in the digest.
docs.set_state: Put the node in one of its `states`: the state's table is patched over the components it names, and `on_state_changed(from, to)` follows. A node already in that state is left alone.
docs.set_tint: Multiply a colour into everything the node and its subtree draw, alpha included, one meaning untinted. A renderable's own `color` is the node's alone; this is the one that inherits.
docs.set_visible: Show or hide the node and everything under it, emitting `visibility_changed` with the new value when the flag moves. Physics is untouched: a hidden collider still collides.
docs.set_z_index: Put the node and its subtree on a draw layer: higher draws later. It adds to the parent's layer unless `z_as_relative = false` makes it absolute.
docs.sibling_index: Where the node sits among its parent's children, counting from zero; 0 at the root.
docs.stable_id: The node's stable id: what a scene file declared, or what it was given when it was spawned. Survives rename and reparent, which a path does not.
docs.state: The state the node is in, or "" for the pose the scene gave it.
docs.tags: The names the node is filed under, sorted.
docs.ticking: Whether the node ticks this frame, its process mode and the game's pause together.
docs.tint: The node's own tint as r, g, b, a channel floats; an ancestor's multiplies into it on the way to the screen.
docs.translate: Move the node by an offset in its parent's space, given as three numbers or one vector.
docs.visible: Whether the node itself is set to draw; an ancestor may still hide it.
docs.visible_in_tree: What the renderer sees: false when the node or any ancestor is hidden.
docs.z_index: The node's own draw layer, added to its parent's unless set absolute.

modules.doc: What spans both physics worlds: pausing, sleeping, tuning and clearing. Bodies and colliders live in `physics2d` and `physics3d`.

docs.clear: Remove every body and collider from both worlds, as a play-in-editor session does on stop.
docs.counters: What each world's last step spent its time on, as `#{ physics3d, physics2d }`, each with every timer rapier keeps, in milliseconds (`step_ms`; the stages `update_ms`, `user_changes_ms`, `collision_detection_ms`, `island_construction_ms`, `island_constraints_ms`, `solver_ms`, `ccd_ms`; collision detection's `broad_phase_ms`, `final_broad_phase_ms`, `narrow_phase_ms`; the solver's `velocity_resolution_ms`, `velocity_assembly_ms`, `velocity_assembly_bodies_ms`, `velocity_assembly_constraints_ms`, `velocity_update_ms`, `velocity_writeback_ms`; continuous collision's `ccd_time_of_impact_ms`, `ccd_solver_ms`, `ccd_broad_phase_ms`, `ccd_narrow_phase_ms`) and every count (`contact_pair_count`, `constraint_count`, `contact_count`, `ccd_substep_count`). The first call turns rapier's profilers on, so the numbers arrive from the step after it.
docs.debug_draw: What the debug renderer is drawing now, as a table of `enabled`, one flag per mode and `nodes`.
docs.quarantined: What rapier disabled in each world's last step because a position, velocity or shape stopped being a number, as `#{ physics3d, physics2d }`, each `#{ bodies, colliders, soft_bodies }` lists of nodes. Empty lists are the normal answer.
docs.set_debug_draw: Draw the physics world over the scene: `true` for the usual shapes, or a table naming modes (`#{ colliders = true, impulse_joints = true }`): `colliders`, `aabbs`, `axes`, `impulse_joints`, `multibody_joints`, `contacts`, `solver_contacts`, `soft_bodies`, `pseudo_normals`, `soft_volume_contacts`, `soft_stress` (soft-body edges coloured by load), with `nodes`, a list of nodes whose bodies, colliders, joints, contacts and soft bodies alone are drawn. `[physics.debug]` holds the colours and lengths.
docs.set_paused: Stop or resume stepping both worlds; nodes keep their poses.
docs.set_ragdoll_influence: How much of the ragdoll's simulated pose the rig's bones take, 0 to 1: 0 leaves the clip in charge while the bodies simulate unseen, 1 goes limp. Tween it to fall over and get back up.
docs.set_sleeping_allowed: Allow or forbid resting bodies falling asleep, in both worlds and for bodies added later.
docs.set_threads: How many threads the solver may use, from a script's `init`: rayon's pool is built once, before the first step, and a call after that says so and changes nothing. `[physics] threads` in `project.toml` does the same and outranks nothing -- an `init` that asks wins. The default is one less than the machine reports, capped at eight.
docs.set_tuning: Change how the solver behaves: `solver_iterations`, `length_unit`, `ccd_substeps`, contact softness, the `soft_*` rows and a `soft_recovery` table, the keys `[physics]` takes. A key at the top reaches both worlds; a `3d` or `2d` table holds keys for that world alone, which win over the top. Every value here changes results, so a recording only replays against the same numbers: prefer `[physics]`, `[physics.3d]` and `[physics.2d]` in project.toml.
docs.sleeping_allowed: Whether resting bodies are allowed to fall asleep.
docs.threads: How many threads the solver is using. One in a browser, unless the page is the threaded template and called `initThreadPool`.
docs.tuning: The solver settings each world is running with, as `#{ "3d", "2d" }`, each holding every key `set_tuning` takes, `soft_recovery` included.

modules.doc: The 2D rigid-body world: bodies and colliders on nodes, their velocities, raycasts and overlap queries. `physics` holds what spans both worlds.

docs.aabb: The world-space box the collider currently occupies, as its two opposite corners.
docs.active_bodies: Every node whose body is awake this step: what a game loops over when it wants to touch only what is moving.
docs.add_constant_force: Push the body every step until the constant force is set back to zero; unlike an impulse this is spread over time.
docs.add_constant_force_at_point: Push at a world point every step, which also turns the body.
docs.add_constant_torque: Turn the body every step until the constant torque is set back to zero.
docs.add_particle_force: Push one particle with `force` each step until `reset_softbody_forces`.
docs.add_softbody_force: Push every free particle with `force` each step until `reset_softbody_forces`.
docs.angular_velocity: How fast the body is spinning, in radians per second.
docs.apply_force: Push the body for the next step only; `add_constant_force` keeps pushing.
docs.apply_force_at_point: Push at a world point for the next step only, which also turns the body.
docs.apply_impulse: Add an instant change in momentum, as if the body were struck.
docs.apply_impulse_at_point: Strike the body at a world point, which spins it as well as moves it.
docs.apply_softbody_impulse: Change every free particle's velocity by `impulse` at once, as a kick to the whole body.
docs.apply_softbody_impulse_at: Strike the particles within `radius` of `point`, less the further they are; a radius of 0 strikes them all.
docs.apply_softbody_radial_impulse: Push the particles within `radius` away from `center`, as a blast does.
docs.apply_torque: Turn the body for the next step only; `add_constant_torque` keeps turning it.
docs.apply_torque_impulse: Add an instant change in angular momentum, as if the body were spun.
docs.attach_particle: Tie one particle to a node's rigid body where it is now: the body and the particle pull on each other.
docs.bodies: Every node with a rigid body, sorted.
docs.broad_phase_aabb: The box the broad phase files the collider under, which also reaches ahead by its body's speculative_distance.
docs.closest_point: The closest point on any collider to a world point.
docs.closest_points: The nearest point on each of two nodes' colliders, as `#{ a, b }`; nothing when they overlap.
docs.collider_mass: What this collider weighs, density and size together.
docs.collider_mass_properties: What this collider adds to its body, in its own space: `#{ mass, center_of_mass, inertia }`.
docs.collider_mesh: A voxel collider's outline as points and the segments between them, `#{ points, indices }`, for drawing it or for spawning the pieces it broke into.
docs.collider_volume: How much area the shape encloses.
docs.collision_aabb: The box the narrow phase tests the collider in: its shape's box grown by its collision_margin and the world's prediction distance.
docs.combine_voxels: Tell two voxel colliders on one lattice about each other's cells, so a body sliding from one onto the other does not catch on the seam. Both must share a cell size and a rotation.
docs.constant_force: The force every step integrates until it is set back to zero.
docs.constant_torque: The torque every step integrates until it is set back to zero.
docs.contacts: Every contact point on this node's collider this step: `#{ node, point, normal, impulse }` each. Empty for a sensor, which has no contacts by definition.
docs.crop_voxels: Empty every cell outside the cells from `(min_x, min_y)` to `(max_x, max_y)`, both included. A range holding no filled cell leaves the grid as it was.
docs.cut_softbody: Cut the body along a blade at once, as `softbody_crossing` reads it; answers a record for each piece it changed, the one `on_tear` hears.
docs.detach_particle: Untie one particle from every body it was attached to; answers whether it was attached.
docs.distance: The gap between two nodes' colliders, zero when they touch.
docs.effective_angular_inertia: The inertia the solver turns: zero with rotation locked, and on any body that is not dynamic.
docs.effective_dominance: The dominance rapier will use for this body: its own group, or the rank every non-dynamic body outranks with.
docs.effective_mass: The mass the solver pushes against along each world axis: zero along a locked axis, and on any body that is not dynamic.
docs.handles: The rapier handles behind this node, its body and its colliders, as `#{ body, colliders }` of index and generation pairs. For matching a log line against rapier's own output.
docs.has_pending_tears: Whether some edge or cell is marked to tear at the end of the next step.
docs.heightfield_hole: Whether a heightfield segment has no ground.
docs.intersects: Whether two nodes' colliders overlap right now, sensor or not.
docs.is_ccd_active: Whether the body moved fast enough last step for rapier to sweep it, with or without continuous_collision.
docs.is_moving: Whether the body is awake and actually going somewhere.
docs.is_on_floor: Whether the last move ended with ground under the character's feet.
docs.is_sleeping: Whether the body is asleep and being skipped.
docs.joint_force: The force and the torque the joint held through the last step, `#{ force, torque }`. An articulation has none to read, and says so.
docs.joint_state: What the joint is doing: `#{ status, angle, limit_impulses, motor_impulses, coordinates, velocities }`, as in 3D: `status` is `enabled`, `disabled`, `body_disabled` or `waiting`; `angle` is a hinge's turn in radians; an articulation adds each free axis's coordinate and velocity.
docs.kinetic_energy: The body's kinetic energy, for a rest test the solver agrees with.
docs.linear_velocity: How fast the body is travelling, in units per second.
docs.local_center_of_mass: Where the body's whole mass sits, in the body's own space.
docs.max_contact_impulse: The hardest contact this body took in the last step, zero when nothing touched it.
docs.move_character: Move the character by an offset, sliding along walls, climbing steps and staying on the ground: returns `#{ x, y, on_floor, sliding, collisions }`, each collision carrying the same fields as in 3D. Every solid collider of the character is swept. Call it from fixed_update.
docs.next_position: The pose a kinematic body has been told to move to, as `#{ position, rotation }`.
docs.overlap_aabb: Every collider whose bounds meet an axis-aligned box.
docs.overlap_point: Every collider containing a world point: what a mouse click asks.
docs.overlap_shape: Every collider a shape overlaps where it stands.
docs.overlaps: The nodes this one currently intersects; rapier reports a pair only when one of the two colliders is a sensor.
docs.pin_particle: Hold one particle where it is, which is how a cloth hangs from a hook.
docs.pose_in_body: Where the collider sits in its body's frame, as `#{ position, rotation }`; nothing for a collider with no body.
docs.potential_energy: The body's gravitational potential energy over one step.
docs.predict_position: Where the body will be after `dt` seconds at its current velocity, as `#{ position, rotation }`.
docs.predict_position_with_forces: The same, with the forces already applied taken into account: where a thrust or a spring will have put it.
docs.ragdoll: Build a 2D ragdoll from the rig under this node: a body and a shape per bone, hinged to its parent's with the hinge's zero at the pose the rig is in. Options as in 3D, with `shape` one of `capsule`, `rectangle` or `circle` and `axes` records on `rotation`. Answers the body nodes it made.
docs.raycast: The first collider a ray meets: `#{ from = [x, y], dir = [x, y], max = 100.0, filter = #{ exclude = node } }`. Returns `#{ node, point, normal, distance }`, or nothing.
docs.raycast_all: Every collider a ray meets, nearest first.
docs.remove_joint: Undo the node's joint, leaving both bodies free.
docs.reset_follow: Forget what a `pid` follow summed, so it pulls from now as if it had just started.
docs.reset_plasticity: Undo every permanent set the body took: rest lengths, rest angles and rest shapes go back to how it was built, and it springs back from where it is.
docs.reset_softbody_forces: Take back every force `add_softbody_force` and `add_particle_force` gave the body.
docs.set_angular_velocity: Set how fast the body spins, in radians per second.
docs.set_cell_tear_resistance: The same for one cell's tear strain.
docs.set_collider: Replace the node's collider from a `collider2d` table: `kind`, `radius`, `size`, `friction`, and the rest of the component's own vocabulary.
docs.set_constant_force: Replace the constant force with this one; zero stops the push.
docs.set_constant_torque: Replace the constant torque with this one; zero stops the turn.
docs.set_edge_tear_resistance: How many times the material's threshold one edge takes to tear; 1 is the material's.
docs.set_gravity: Set the 2D world's gravity, in units per second squared.
docs.set_heightfield_hole: Remove or restore one segment of a heightfield's ground, numbered from the first height.
docs.set_joint_limits: Set how far one of the joint's free axes may travel; equal values lift the limit. Rewrites that axis's `axes` record.
docs.set_linear_velocity: Set how fast the body travels, in units per second.
docs.set_motor_position: Drive one of the joint's free axes towards an angle or a distance, with a spring's stiffness and damping. Rewrites that axis's `axes` record.
docs.set_motor_velocity: Drive one of the joint's free axes towards a speed: how a wheel is powered. Rewrites that axis's `axes` record.
docs.set_particle_damaged: Mark one particle as damaged or mend it: a damaged particle tears as an outside one does, which seeds where a crack starts.
docs.set_particle_position: Put one particle at `at` with no change of velocity.
docs.set_particle_target: Move a held particle to `at` over the next step, with the velocity that takes, which is how a cloth is dragged.
docs.set_particle_velocity: Set one particle's velocity; a held one keeps moving at it.
docs.set_softbody: Build the node's soft body from a `softbody2d` table: `kind`, the shape rows, and the material rows.
docs.set_voxel: Fill or empty one cell of a voxel collider: digging a hole, or building a wall, while the game runs.
docs.set_voxel_size: Resize every cell of a voxel collider, keeping which cells are filled.
docs.shapecast: Sweep a shape along a direction until it hits something: a thick raycast.
docs.sleep: Put the body to sleep now.
docs.softbody_area: How much area the body and every piece torn off it enclose right now, against `softbody_rest_area` for how far it is squeezed.
docs.softbody_attachments: Every particle tied to a rigid body, as `#{ particle, body, anchor, impulse }`: the anchor in the body's own space, and the impulse the tie pulled with in the last substep.
docs.softbody_boundary: The body's surface as particle indices: segments in 2D, triangles in 3D.
docs.softbody_cell: Everything one cell holds: `#{ particles, rest_volume, stiffness_scale, tear_resistance, stress, plastic_stretch }`; `stress` is its strain as a fraction of `tear_strain`, `plastic_stretch` the rows of the permanent stretch of its rest shape.
docs.softbody_cells: Every cell as its particle indices: triangles in 2D, tetrahedra in 3D.
docs.softbody_center: The centre of mass of the body and its pieces, which is where it is when a deformable body has no one position.
docs.softbody_contacts: What the body's surface touched in the last step: `#{ edges, vertices, volumes }`. Each edge and vertex contact with another soft body or itself is a pair of world points, the two witnesses; each volume contact is `#{ center, normal, volume }`.
docs.softbody_crossing: The edges and cells a blade meets, `#{ edges, cells }`, without cutting: the blade is a segment's two points in 2D, a triangle's three in 3D.
docs.softbody_edge: Everything one edge holds: `#{ particles, kind, rest_length, initial_rest_length, plastic_strain, tension_only, softness_hz, softness_damping_ratio, tear_resistance, impulse, stress }`; `kind` is `structural` or `bending`, and the softness is the edge's own or its kind's from the material.
docs.softbody_edges: Every edge as the two particle indices it joins, in the order `softbody_stress` reports them.
docs.softbody_mass: What the whole body weighs, every piece included.
docs.softbody_particle: Everything one particle holds: `#{ position, velocity, force, target, rest_position, initial_rest_position, mass, inverse_mass, pinned, damaged, on_surface }`. `force` is what `add_particle_force` keeps on it, `target` where a held particle is going (nil when none), the two rest positions are relative to the rest centre of mass, before and after plastic flow, and `inverse_mass` is 0 while it is held.
docs.softbody_particle_radius: How thick the particles are: what was asked for, or what the layout worked out.
docs.softbody_particles: How many particles the body has, every piece torn off it included: a generator decides, not the author.
docs.softbody_position: Where one particle is, in world space.
docs.softbody_rest_area: How much they enclose at rest.
docs.softbody_sleeping: Whether the body has come to rest and stopped being simulated.
docs.softbody_stress: Each edge's load as a fraction of its tear threshold, smoothed over `tear_smoothing`: 0 slack, 1 tearing; the larger of its stretch over `tear_strain` and its force over `tear_force`, and 0 while neither is set.
docs.softbody_velocity: How fast one particle is moving, in world space.
docs.softbody_volume_pieces: Each closed piece of the surface whose volume is held, as `#{ particles, rest_volume, volume }`; an open sheet has none.
docs.solve_ik: Move a reduced-coordinates chain so its last link reaches a world position, leaving every joint inside its limits. Options: `rotation` (radians to turn the link to), `constrain` (the world axes to match: `x`, `y`, `rotation`; the translation by default, every axis when `rotation` is given), `damping` (1.0), `iterations` (10), `tolerance` (0.001).
docs.swept_aabb: The box the collider covers over the next fixed step, from where it is to where its body's velocity and forces carry it.
docs.tear_cell: Tear one cell at the end of the next step: a particle near its middle splits across its main stretch.
docs.tear_edge: Tear one edge at the end of the next step.
docs.tear_softbody: Tear the given edges and cells at once; answers a record for each piece it changed: `#{ pieces, edges, cells, removed_edges, split_particles, inserted_particles, piece_particles, clusters, moved_joints }`, the one `on_tear` hears. Particle indices are the torn piece's own; `split_particles` holds `[copy, source]` pairs, `clusters` `#{ source, cluster, keeps_proxy }`, and `moved_joints` the joint nodes a cluster split moved.
docs.teleport: Move the body to a world position at once, clearing its velocity: what assigning the node's position cannot do, because the step writes that back every tick. `#{ rotation = angle }` turns it too, in radians.
docs.time_of_impact: When two moving colliders would meet, given each one's velocity: `#{ velocity_a = [..], velocity_b = [..], max_time = 1.0 }`. Nothing when they never do.
docs.time_since_can_sleep: Seconds the body has spent under its sleep thresholds; it sleeps once this reaches time_to_sleep.
docs.total_inertia: The body's resistance to spin, colliders included.
docs.total_mass: The body's total mass: its `mass` when it states one, or what its colliders weigh.
docs.unpin_particle: Let a held particle go; it keeps the velocity it had.
docs.velocity_at_point: How fast a world point on the body is moving, spin included.
docs.voxel: Whether one cell of a voxel collider is filled.
docs.voxel_at: The cell a world position falls in, as two whole numbers.
docs.voxel_size: How big one cell of a voxel collider is, along each axis.
docs.wake_all: Wake every sleeping body in the 2D world.
docs.wake_softbody: Start simulating a resting body again.
docs.wake_up: Wake the body, so the next step moves it.
docs.world_center_of_mass: Where the body's whole mass sits, in world space.
