docs.is_on_floor: Whether the last move ended with ground under the character's feet.
docs.is_sleeping: Whether the body is asleep and being skipped.
docs.joint_force: The force and the torque the joint held through the last step, `#{ force, torque }`: what `break_force` and `break_torque` are measured against. An articulation has none to read, and says so.
docs.joint_state: What the joint is doing: `#{ status, angle, limit_impulses, motor_impulses, coordinates, velocities }`. `status` is `enabled`, `disabled`, `body_disabled` (a body at either end is disabled) or `waiting` (its other end is not in the scene yet); `angle` is a hinge's turn in radians; the impulse maps hold each free axis's last limit and motor impulse; an articulation adds each free axis's coordinate and velocity.
docs.kinetic_energy: The body's kinetic energy, for a rest test the solver agrees with.
docs.linear_velocity: How fast the body is travelling, in units per second.
docs.local_center_of_mass: Where the body's whole mass sits, in the body's own space.
docs.max_contact_impulse: The hardest contact this node took in the last step, zero when nothing touched it: a damage threshold in one number.
docs.move_character: Move the character by an offset, sliding along walls, climbing steps and staying on the ground: returns `#{ x, y, z, on_floor, sliding, collisions }`, each collision `#{ node, point, normal, own_point, own_normal, position, applied, remaining, distance, status, subshape }`: the hit on the obstacle and on the character in world space, where the character stood, how much of the move was done and left, how far it swept, how the sweep ended (`converged`, `out_of_iterations`, `failed`, `penetrating`) and which part of the obstacle's shape it met. Every solid collider of the character is swept. Call it from fixed_update. It reads the world the step just wrote.
docs.next_position: The pose a kinematic body has been told to move to, as `#{ position, rotation }`.
docs.overlap_aabb: Every collider whose bounds meet an axis-aligned box; cheaper and looser than shape_hits.
docs.overlap_point: Every collider containing a world point.
docs.overlap_shape: Every collider a shape overlaps where it stands: an explosion's reach, a melee arc.
docs.overlaps: The nodes this one currently intersects; rapier reports a pair only when one of the two colliders is a sensor.
docs.pin_particle: Hold one particle where it is, which is how a cloth hangs from a hook.
docs.pose_in_body: Where the collider sits in its body's frame, as `#{ position, rotation }`; nothing for a collider with no body.
docs.potential_energy: The body's gravitational potential energy over one step.
docs.predict_position: Where the body will be after `dt` seconds at its current velocity, as `#{ position, rotation }`.
docs.predict_position_with_forces: The same, with the forces already applied taken into account: where a thrust or a spring will have put it.
docs.ragdoll: Build a 3D ragdoll from the rig under this node: a body and a shape per bone, held to its parent's by a ball socket whose zero is the pose the rig is in. Options: `shape` (`capsule`, `box` or `sphere`), `thickness` (the capsule's radius and the box's half width, as a fraction of bone length), `density`, `friction`, `restitution`, `collision_layer` and `collision_mask` (layer numbers) for the shapes; `linear_damping`, `angular_damping`, `gravity_scale` and `continuous_collision` for the bodies; `axes` (joint3d `axes` records, on `rotation_x`, `rotation_y`, `rotation_z`: twist and swing limits), `articulation` and `collide_connected` for the joints; `drive` (`none`, or `motors`: a position motor on every turn towards the built pose, of `stiffness` 100 and `damping` 20 unless given; or `follow`: a `follow3d` on every body towards its bone, so the bodies chase the clip, its keys in a `follow` table); and `influence`. Answers the body nodes it made.
docs.raycast: The first collider a ray meets: `#{ from = [x, y, z], dir = [x, y, z], max = 100.0, filter = #{ exclude = node, only = "dynamic" } }`. Returns `#{ node, point, normal, distance }`, or nothing.
docs.raycast_all: Every collider a ray meets, nearest first.
docs.remove_joint: Undo the node's joint, leaving both bodies free.
docs.reset_follow: Forget what a `pid` follow summed, so it pulls from now as if it had just started.
docs.reset_plasticity: Undo every permanent set the body took: rest lengths, rest angles and rest shapes go back to how it was built, and it springs back from where it is.
docs.reset_softbody_forces: Take back every force `add_softbody_force` and `add_particle_force` gave the body.
docs.set_angular_velocity: Set how fast the body spins, in radians per second about each axis.
docs.set_brake: How hard this wheel brakes, as an impulse; ignored while its engine force is not 0.
docs.set_cell_tear_resistance: The same for one cell's tear strain.
docs.set_collider: Replace the node's collider from a `collider3d` table: `kind`, `radius`, `size`, `friction`, and the rest of the component's own vocabulary.
docs.set_constant_force: Replace the constant force with this one; zero stops the push.
docs.set_constant_torque: Replace the constant torque with this one; zero stops the turn.
docs.set_edge_tear_resistance: How many times the material's threshold one edge takes to tear; 1 is the material's.
docs.set_engine_force: How hard this wheel drives, in newtons; negative reverses.
docs.set_gravity: Set the 3D world's gravity, in units per second squared.
docs.set_heightfield_hole: Remove or restore the ground of one heightfield cell, named by the row and column of its first corner.
docs.set_joint_limits: Set how far one of the joint's free axes may travel, in radians about a rotation axis and units along a linear one; equal values lift the limit. Rewrites that axis's `axes` record.
docs.set_linear_velocity: Set how fast the body travels, in units per second.
docs.set_motor_position: Drive one of the joint's free axes towards an angle or a distance, with a spring's stiffness and damping. Rewrites that axis's `axes` record.
docs.set_motor_velocity: Drive one of the joint's free axes towards a speed: how a wheel is powered or a door swings itself shut. Rewrites that axis's `axes` record.
docs.set_particle_damaged: Mark one particle as damaged or mend it: a damaged particle tears as an outside one does, which seeds where a crack starts.
docs.set_particle_position: Put one particle at `at` with no change of velocity.
docs.set_particle_target: Move a held particle to `at` over the next step, with the velocity that takes, which is how a cloth is dragged.
docs.set_particle_velocity: Set one particle's velocity; a held one keeps moving at it.
docs.set_softbody: Build the node's soft body from a `softbody3d` table: `kind`, the shape rows, and the material rows.
docs.set_voxel: Fill or empty one cell of a voxel collider: digging a hole, or building a wall, while the game runs.
docs.set_voxel_size: Resize every cell of a voxel collider, keeping which cells are filled.
docs.set_wheel_rotation: Set how far the wheel has turned about its axle, in radians: the angle `wheel_state` reads as `rotation`.
docs.shapecast: Sweep a shape along a direction until it hits something: a thick raycast, and how a camera avoids walls.
docs.sleep: Put the body to sleep now.
docs.softbody_attachments: Every particle tied to a rigid body, as `#{ particle, body, anchor, impulse }`: the anchor in the body's own space, and the impulse the tie pulled with in the last substep.
docs.softbody_boundary: The body's surface as particle indices: segments in 2D, triangles in 3D.
docs.softbody_cell: Everything one cell holds: `#{ particles, rest_volume, stiffness_scale, tear_resistance, stress, plastic_stretch }`; `stress` is its strain as a fraction of `tear_strain`, `plastic_stretch` the rows of the permanent stretch of its rest shape.
docs.softbody_cells: Every cell as its particle indices: triangles in 2D, tetrahedra in 3D.
docs.softbody_center: The centre of mass of the body and its pieces, which is where it is when a deformable body has no one position.
docs.softbody_contacts: What the body's surface touched in the last step: `#{ edges, vertices, volumes }`. Each edge and vertex contact with another soft body or itself is a pair of world points, the two witnesses; each volume contact is `#{ center, normal, volume }`.
docs.softbody_crossing: The edges and cells a blade meets, `#{ edges, cells }`, without cutting: the blade is a segment's two points in 2D, a triangle's three in 3D.
docs.softbody_dihedral: Everything one hinge holds: `#{ particles, rest_angle, initial_rest_angle, plastic_set }`, angles in radians; `plastic_set` is how far its rest angle has flowed from the one it was built with.
docs.softbody_dihedrals: Every bending hinge between two surface triangles, as four particle indices: the shared edge, then the two opposite particles.
docs.softbody_edge: Everything one edge holds: `#{ particles, kind, rest_length, initial_rest_length, plastic_strain, tension_only, softness_hz, softness_damping_ratio, tear_resistance, impulse, stress }`; `kind` is `structural` or `bending`, and the softness is the edge's own or its kind's from the material.
docs.softbody_edges: Every edge as the two particle indices it joins, in the order `softbody_stress` reports them.
docs.softbody_mass: What the whole body weighs, every piece included.
docs.softbody_particle: Everything one particle holds: `#{ position, velocity, force, target, rest_position, initial_rest_position, mass, inverse_mass, pinned, damaged, on_surface }`. `force` is what `add_particle_force` keeps on it, `target` where a held particle is going (nil when none), the two rest positions are relative to the rest centre of mass, before and after plastic flow, and `inverse_mass` is 0 while it is held.
docs.softbody_particle_radius: How thick the particles are: what was asked for, or what the layout worked out.
docs.softbody_particles: How many particles the body has, every piece torn off it included: a generator decides, not the author.
docs.softbody_position: Where one particle is, in world space.
docs.softbody_rest_volume: How much they enclose at rest.
docs.softbody_sleeping: Whether the body has come to rest and stopped being simulated.
docs.softbody_stress: Each edge's load as a fraction of its tear threshold, smoothed over `tear_smoothing`: 0 slack, 1 tearing; the larger of its stretch over `tear_strain` and its force over `tear_force`, and 0 while neither is set.
docs.softbody_velocity: How fast one particle is moving, in world space.
docs.softbody_volume: How much space the body and every piece torn off it enclose right now, against `softbody_rest_volume` for how far it is squeezed.
docs.softbody_volume_pieces: Each closed piece of the surface whose volume is held, as `#{ particles, rest_volume, volume }`; an open sheet has none.
docs.solve_ik: Move a reduced-coordinates chain so its last link reaches a world position, leaving every joint inside its limits. Options: `rotation` (euler radians to turn the link to), `constrain` (the world axes to match: `x`, `y`, `z`, `rotation_x`, `rotation_y`, `rotation_z`; the translation by default, every axis when `rotation` is given), `damping` (1.0), `iterations` (10), `tolerance` (0.001).
docs.speed: The chassis's whole speed at the last step, negative while it moves against its forward axis: rapier's own reading, where `vehicle_speed` is the part along the forward axis alone.
docs.swept_aabb: The box the collider covers over the next fixed step, from where it is to where its body's velocity and forces carry it.
docs.tear_cell: Tear one cell at the end of the next step: a particle near its middle splits across its main stretch.
docs.tear_edge: Tear one edge at the end of the next step.
docs.tear_softbody: Tear the given edges and cells at once; answers a record for each piece it changed: `#{ pieces, edges, cells, removed_edges, split_particles, inserted_particles, piece_particles, clusters, moved_joints }`, the one `on_tear` hears. Particle indices are the torn piece's own; `split_particles` holds `[copy, source]` pairs, `clusters` `#{ source, cluster, keeps_proxy }`, and `moved_joints` the joint nodes a cluster split moved.
docs.teleport: Move the body to a world position at once, clearing its velocity: what assigning the node's position cannot do, because the step writes that back every tick. `#{ rotation = [x, y, z] }` turns it too, in Euler radians.
docs.time_of_impact: When two moving colliders would meet, given each one's velocity: `#{ velocity_a = [..], velocity_b = [..], max_time = 1.0 }`. Nothing when they never do.
docs.time_since_can_sleep: Seconds the body has spent under its sleep thresholds; it sleeps once this reaches time_to_sleep.
docs.total_inertia: The body's resistance to spin about each of its principal axes, colliders included.
docs.total_inertia_rotation: How those principal axes are turned in the body's own space, as Euler radians, x first.
docs.total_mass: The body's total mass: its `mass` when it states one, or what its colliders weigh.
docs.unpin_particle: Let a held particle go; it keeps the velocity it had.
docs.vehicle_speed: How fast the chassis is going along its forward axis, in units per second.
docs.velocity_at_point: How fast a world point on the body is moving, spin included.
docs.voxel: Whether one cell of a voxel collider is filled.
docs.voxel_at: The cell a world position falls in, as three whole numbers.
docs.voxel_size: How big one cell of a voxel collider is, along each axis.
docs.wake_all: Wake every sleeping body in the 3D world.
docs.wake_softbody: Start simulating a resting body again.
docs.wake_up: Wake the body, so the next step moves it.
docs.wheel_state: What the last step did with this wheel: `#{ rotation, suspension_force, in_contact, engine_force, brake, steering, forward_impulse, side_impulse, contact_normal, contact_point, suspension_length, ray_origin, ground, center, suspension, axle }`. `suspension_force` is what the suspension pushed with, after `suspension_max_force`; the two impulses are the friction rapier applied along and across the wheel; the contact, the ray's start, the wheel's centre and its suspension and axle directions are world space, after steering; `ground` is the node the ray hit, or nil.
docs.world_center_of_mass: Where the body's whole mass sits, in world space.

modules.name: physics3d

modules.doc: Store services every platform shares: sign-in, achievements, leaderboards, cloud saves. A call answers later on `on_platform_event` with a map whose `kind` is `signed_in`, `signed_out`, `done`, `scores`, `read`, `error` or `unsupported`, each an `EVENT_*` constant.

docs.backend: The name of the loaded store, or "none".
docs.cloud_read: Read a value the store syncs between the player's devices.
docs.cloud_write: Write a value for the store to sync between the player's devices.
docs.player: Who the store says is playing, or nil before a sign-in has landed.
docs.scores: Read a leaderboard's entries. The options take `count`, `start` (a rank, from 1), `scope` ("global" or "friends") and `period` ("today", "week" or "all_time").
docs.set_presence: Say what the player is doing, where the store shows it.
docs.sign_in: Ask the store who is playing, and return the id its answer carries. A node given here keeps hearing: a later sign-out reaches the same method.
docs.submit_score: Post a score to a leaderboard.

modules.name: platform

modules.doc: The projects this machine has opened, the templates a new one starts from, and the folder picker the OS provides. What the editor's start screen is made of.

docs.copy_example: Copy one example into `into` under its own name, so the shipped one stays as it is. Answers `{ path, name }`, or `{ error }`.
docs.create: Write a new project at `path` from a template id, or from nothing when the id is empty. Answers `{ path, name }`, or `{ error }`.
docs.editor_data_directory: The editor's per-user folder, `<data>/balaur-editor` beside the games' `<data>/balaur/<name>`: `editor.toml`, `projects.toml`, `sessions/` and `themes/`. Made on first ask.
docs.examples: The example projects shipped beside the editor: `{ id, name, note, cover, path }` each, where `cover` is a picture the editor's own project holds, or empty.
docs.forget: Drop one project from the list. The folder is not touched.
docs.home: Where a new project goes unless the reader says otherwise: the home directory on a desktop, and the app's own writable directory where there is no such thing.
docs.in_tab: Whether this editor runs in a browser tab, where the page holds the projects and opening one is its call rather than this screen's.
docs.open: Remember `path` and start the editor on it, then ask this one to quit. Answers `{ error }` when there is no project there.
docs.pick_directory: Open the OS folder picker and answer what was chosen, or `()` when it was dismissed. Blocks while the dialog is up, and answers `()` on a platform with no picker.
docs.recent: The projects opened on this machine, newest first: `{ path, name, opened, exists }` each, where `opened` is a Unix time in seconds and `exists` says whether the folder is still there.
docs.templates: What a new project may start from: `{ id, note }` each, read from the editor's own library.
docs.use_data: Keep `save::` slots and the device id in the user data directory of the game named `name`, and let `fs` reach it, so a game played here and run alone share saves and a device login. Nil goes back to the editor's own. Answers the directory, or nil.
docs.version: The version of the binary the editor is running in.

modules.name: project

modules.doc: The engine's one deterministic PCG32 stream: the same seed draws the same numbers on every platform, and a replay reproduces every draw.

docs.float: A float from the deterministic engine stream, uniform in `[0, 1)`.
docs.int: A whole number from the deterministic engine stream, uniform in `[low, high]`, both ends included.
docs.range: A float from the deterministic engine stream, uniform in `[low, high)`: the two arguments.
docs.seed: Restart the deterministic engine stream at the given seed, so every draw after it repeats.
docs.uuid: A version-4 UUID drawn from the deterministic engine stream, so a replay makes the same ids; not for anything that must be unique across machines.

modules.name: random

modules.doc: Regular expressions, the `regex-lite` dialect: no look-around or back-references. A pattern is compiled on every call; a match is `#{ start, end, text, groups }` with byte offsets and one string per capture group, nil for a group that took no part.

docs.escape: `text` with every metacharacter escaped, so it matches itself.
docs.matches: Whether the pattern matches anywhere in `text`.
docs.replace: `text` with the first match replaced, or every match when `all` is true; `$1` and `${name}` in `with` stand for groups.

modules.name: regex

signatures.replace: (pattern: string, text: string, with: string, all: bool?) -> string

modules.doc: Which build of the engine this is, what the channels are publishing, and replacing this install with another. The editor's Engine tab and About sheet; `balaur update` is the same code.

docs.channels: Every release line a build may follow, in the order a version moves through them.
docs.check: Read the release feed on a thread. `listen` hears `{ kind: "listed", rows }`, newest first, each `{ tag, id, channel, when, current, order, download }`: `order` is `newer`, `older` or `same` than this build, empty where they do not order, and `download` is the zipped app a macOS bundle fetches instead. `{ kind: "failed", job: "check", message }` when the feed could not be read. False while a recording plays.
docs.install: Replace this install with what that channel or tag holds, on a thread; `allow_downgrade = true` lets an older build replace a newer one. `listen` hears `downloading` with `done` and `total` bytes, `unpacking`, then `installed` with a `note`, or `failed` with `job: "install"`. Refuses where `installed().held` says why. False while a recording plays.
docs.installed: This build: `{ version, id, channel, tag, source, held }`, where `id` is the build id a release was tagged with, `tag` is the release its assets live under, `source` is true for a build from a checkout, and `held` says why this install cannot replace itself, empty when it can.
docs.listen: Call a method on `node` with every report a check or an install makes: `on_release_event` unless `opts.on_event` names another.

modules.name: release

modules.doc: What a frame is made of: the shape, sprite, mesh or emitter a node draws, the 2D and 3D cameras, the backdrop, debug lines and screenshots. `window` holds the window itself.

docs.bounds: The box the node's geometry covers in its own space, as a centre xyz and half-extents xyz, with a z of zero for a 2D node; nil for a node that draws nothing. A solver's body reports where it is now, not where it was built.
docs.buffer: Every instance as one flat list of floats in Godot's `MultiMesh.buffer` layout: 12 of transform in 3D or 8 in 2D, then 4 of colour and 4 of custom data.
docs.built_mesh: The triangles the node's boolean settled on, as `#{ positions, indices }` ready to be written out as a `mesh` asset; nil when the node draws no built geometry.
docs.camera_2d: The 2D camera this frame: centre xy and zoom in logical pixels per world unit; all zeros with no window.
docs.camera_matrix: The camera's projection*view matrix this frame, 16 numbers column-major; all zeros with no window.
docs.camera_pose: The camera the renderer actually used: eye xyz, target xyz, vertical fov in radians, HiDPI scale.
docs.cell: The tile at a column and row, or -1 for an empty cell or one past the edge.
docs.check_material: Every diagnostic about the material at that path, as `[#{ file, line, column, severity, message }]`; empty when it links.
docs.debug_view: Which channel the viewport is drawing instead of the scene's colour, or empty for the scene as it is.
docs.debug_views: Every channel name `set_debug_view` accepts, as a list.
docs.draw_arc_2d: Stroke an arc between two angles in radians, counter-clockwise from the x axis, for this frame; width is in pixels, and `opts` takes `z_index`.
docs.draw_box: Draw a wireframe box centred at a point, from its three half-extents in world units, for this frame.
docs.draw_capsule: Draw a wireframe capsule centred at a point, `height` being the straight part along y, for this frame.
docs.draw_circle_2d: Fill a circle in world units for this frame, over everything the scene drew; `opts.z_index` places it among the nodes of that index instead.
docs.draw_line_2d: Draw one 2D world-space line for this frame; width is in pixels, and `opts.z_index` places it among the nodes of that index.
docs.draw_line_3d: Draw one 3D world-space line for this frame; the width is in pixels unless perspective scales it with distance.
docs.draw_lines: Draw many 3D lines in one call: eleven numbers a segment, being both ends, an rgb, a width and an on-top flag.
docs.draw_polygon_2d: Fill a convex outline of world-space points for this frame; `geometry2d` cuts a concave one into triangles first. `opts` takes `z_index`.
docs.draw_polyline_2d: Stroke a chain of world-space points for this frame; width is in pixels, and `opts` takes `z_index`.
docs.draw_rect_2d: Fill a rectangle centred at a point, in world units, for this frame; `opts` takes `z_index`.
docs.draw_sphere: Draw a wireframe sphere centred at a point, as three rings in world units, for this frame.
docs.draw_text_2d: Draw a line of text in 2D world space for this frame, shaped by the engine's fonts. `opts` takes the `text2d` keys (`font_size`, `font_weight`, `font_style`, `color`, `text_align`, `markup`, `max_width`, `font_family`, `bitmap_font`, …), `pixels_per_unit` and `z_index`.
docs.draw_text_3d: The same in 3D world space, on a quad that faces the camera. `pixels_per_unit` sizes it, so text a metre away reads the same whatever the font size.
docs.draw_texture_2d: Draw a project image over a rectangle centred at a point, in world units, for this frame; the colour tints it. `opts` takes `z_index`, and `region_origin` and `region_size` in the image's pixels for part of it.
docs.instance_color: The colour one instance draws in.
docs.instance_count: How many instances the node holds.
docs.instance_custom_data: One instance's four floats of custom data, as a colour.
docs.instance_region: One instance's texture rectangle as `[x, y, w, h]` in pixels, or nil when it draws the whole texture.
docs.instance_transform: One instance's transform: a `Transform3d`, or a `Transform2d` on a 2D node.
docs.instances: Every instance as the `multimesh` asset spells it, so `assets.save` writes a scripted layout into a file.
docs.is_on_screen: Whether any of the notifier's box was on screen at the end of the last frame.
docs.material_params: The material's editable rows, one `#{ name, type, value }` per field its linked shader declares; empty when it will not link.
docs.mouse_ray: The picking ray through the mouse position: its origin xyz then its direction xyz, in world units.
docs.mouse_world_2d: The mouse position in 2D world coordinates, for picking.
docs.outline: The outline this node blocks 2D light with, in world space: x then y for each point in turn, with the first repeated at the end when the outline is closed. Empty on a node with no `occluder2d`.
docs.pick_ray: The nearest node with a 3D shape that a world-space ray meets, from its origin xyz and direction xyz.
docs.pick_ray_at: As `pick_ray`, but `node` and `at`, how far along the ray it was met; nil when the ray meets nothing.
docs.populate: Godot's Populate Surface, and a row, a ring or a grid: the instances a layout would write, worked out from `seed`, returned in the `multimesh` asset's shape rather than set. `kind` is `render.POPULATE_SURFACE` with a `surface` node, `POPULATE_ROW` (`count`, `step`), `POPULATE_RING` (`count`, `radius`) or `POPULATE_GRID` (`counts`, `step`); `rotation`, `tilt` and `random_scale` vary each instance, as fractions, around `scale`.
docs.screenshot: Save the next rendered frame as a PNG at a project-relative path. `screenshot_written` goes to every listener with the path once it is on disk, and `screenshot_failed` with `#{ path, error }` when it cannot be, a run with no renderer included.
docs.set_background: Set the colour the viewport is cleared to behind everything drawn, as r, g, b channel floats.
docs.set_box: Draw the node as a box from its three half-extents, in world units, replacing any other 3D shape.
docs.set_buffer: Replace every instance from one flat list in the layout `buffer` answers in, for a Godot port that sets `buffer`. Building the list in a script costs more than one `set_instance_transform` per instance.
docs.set_camera: Point the 3D camera: the eye position xyz, then the world point it looks at, in world units.
docs.set_camera_2d: Point the 2D camera: the world centre xy, then the zoom in logical pixels per world unit.
docs.set_cell: Put one tile at a column and row; a tile below zero clears the cell, and a cell outside the map grows it in that direction. The mesh rebuilds on the next frame.
docs.set_debug_view: Draw one channel of the scene (normals, uv, depth or albedo) instead of its colour; an empty name puts the picture back.
docs.set_grid: Turn the ground grid on or off, and optionally set its step in world units, major-line interval and extent.
docs.set_grid_colors: Set the ground grid's minor line colour then its major line colour, as r, g, b channel floats.
docs.set_instance_color: The colour one instance draws in.
docs.set_instance_count: How many instances the node holds. Those below the count keep where they were; new ones are plain, at the node.
docs.set_instance_custom_data: Four floats a material's shader reads for one instance, as a colour or a list.
docs.set_instance_region: The rectangle of the texture one instance draws, as an origin and a size in texture pixels; a zero size draws all of it. Not drawn yet: `multimesh2d` draws through Balaur's own pipeline, which binds no rectangle per instance.
docs.set_instance_transform: Place one instance with a `Transform3d`, or a `Transform2d` on a 2D node. A shear is kept, as the instance's `basis`.
docs.set_instances: Replace every instance with a list in the `multimesh` asset's shape.
docs.set_rectangle: Draw the node as a rectangle from its two half-extents, in world units, replacing any other 2D shape.
docs.set_shader_preview: Draw the value a shader's line computes for every pixel that reaches it; line 0 puts the picture back.
docs.set_shader_probe: Ask what the previewed line computed at one framebuffer pixel; the answer arrives through `shader_probe` a frame later.
docs.set_sphere: Draw the node as a sphere of the given radius in world units, replacing any other 3D shape.
docs.set_terrain: Paint a terrain value at a column and row and let the tileset's rules pick the tiles, for that cell and the ring around it; below zero clears it.
docs.set_visible_instance_count: How many instances draw, from the first; -1 draws them all.
docs.shader_probe: The four channels the previewed line wrote at the probed pixel, or `()` when nothing has been read yet.
docs.snap_aov: Render the 3D scene once more as `render.AOV_DEPTH` (nearest brightest), `AOV_NORMALS` (world space), `AOV_CAMERA_NORMALS` or `AOV_SEGMENTATION` (a colour per object) and save it as a PNG, announcing it as `screenshot` does. A read-back of the GPU, as `screenshot` is.
docs.stats: What this frame draws: `{ draws, triangles, texture_bytes, textures, nodes }`, where `nodes` is a row per node that drew, each `{ node, draws, triangles, texture_bytes, copies }`. Presentation, never simulation: nothing in the digest reads it.
docs.terrain: The terrain value painted at a column and row, or -1 where nothing was painted.
docs.text_size: The width and height `text` shapes to, in font pixels, with the project's own fonts and never a system face — so a headless run and a windowed one answer the same. A width is presentation: writing one into state puts presentation in the digest.
docs.texture_pixels_per_unit: How many of an image's pixels make a world unit when a sprite says 0: its own `pixels_per_unit` import setting, else 100.
docs.texture_size: An image's width and height in pixels, read from the file's own header.
docs.tile_data: What the tileset says about the tile at a column and row -- its `[tiles.<id>.data]` table -- or nil where the cell is empty or the tile carries none.
docs.trace_texture: The outline of an image's opaque pixels, as `[x, y]` points in a node's own space, ready to be a polygon's `positions`. `opts` takes `threshold` (alpha counted as opaque, 0 to 1, default 0.5), `tolerance` (how many pixels of detail to drop, default 2), `pixels_per_unit` (default 100) and `holes` (every loop, largest first: each other island counter-clockwise and each hole clockwise; default false keeps the largest alone). Counter-clockwise with y up, centred on the origin, the way a sprite at the same `pixels_per_unit` is drawn.
docs.visible_instance_count: How many instances draw; -1 is all of them.

modules.doc: Records what a running game is fed and plays it back. A recording holds each tick's input, network arrivals and events; `balaur run --record` writes one.

docs.divergence_tick: The first tick whose replay did not reproduce the recorded digest, or nil.
docs.events: The events recorded between two ticks, each with its tick, kind, label and data.
docs.header: The loaded recording's project, start time, script fingerprint and how it ended.
docs.info: The same summary for a recording on disk, without loading it.
docs.length: The loaded recording's frame count and the ticks it spans, or nil.
docs.load: Read a recording and put it in front of the engine, paused before its first tick.
docs.marks: The ticks at which one replay source held a non-empty list under a key, and what it held.
docs.pause: Stop between ticks, holding the simulation still while the frame loop keeps drawing.
docs.play: Run the loaded recording, one recorded tick per frame.
docs.record: Start recording into a file; call it before the code it records runs.
docs.recording: The file being recorded into, or nil.
docs.recording_name: A file-safe name for a recording starting now, so a list of them sorts by when they ran.
docs.seek: Run recorded ticks until playback reaches the given tick; forward only.
docs.stop: Close the recording, naming why it ended, and return the file it wrote.
docs.unload: Drop the loaded recording and let the game run live again.

modules.doc: Rollback netcode from a script's side. `input` reads this tick's input, real or predicted; `is_resimulating` is true when a tick runs again after a late input.

docs.input: What that player is doing on the tick being simulated, real or predicted; nil outside a session or for a player it does not know.
docs.is_resimulating: Whether this tick is a re-run of one already simulated, so a script can skip anything it must not do twice.

modules.doc: Save games: a table in, a table out, stored per user. `[save] version` stamps each file; `[save] migrate` names the script whose `migrate_save(version, data)` upgrades older ones.

docs.directory: The directory slots are kept in, not created until something is written.
docs.read: The table in a slot, brought forward to this build's version; nil when the slot was never written. An error when the file was written by a newer build, or when it needs a migration the project declares no script for.
docs.remove: Delete a slot. Not an error when it was not there.
docs.slots: Every slot that has been written, in name order.
docs.version: The save version this build writes, from `[save] version`.
docs.write: Write a table to a named slot, stamped with the project's save version. Written beside the target and renamed over it, so a crash mid-save cannot destroy the last one.

modules.doc: The node tree: its root, lookup by path and instancing, plus the component and preset vocabulary an editor's palette lists.

docs.apply_preset: Add every component a preset names to the node; a part that fails leaves the parts before it in place.
docs.bindable_events: Every event a `[[nodes.bindings.rows]]` row may answer, in the order an editor offers them: the core hooks, and on a node the `emitted:` events it and its components announce.
docs.binding_actions: Every action a binding row may do, in the order an editor offers them.
docs.component_expects: The components a component type needs something from, for ordering or grouping its sections; nil for a name nothing registered.
docs.component_properties: What a component's `apply` would receive for `params`: the schema's defaults with a partial table merged over them. This is how a tool compares two spellings of the same component.
docs.component_schema: A component type's property schema as a table; nil for a name nothing registered.
docs.component_tags: The facets a component type is filed under, for filtering a palette; nil for a name nothing registered.
docs.component_types: The names of every registered component type, not the components on any node.
docs.get_node: The node at an `A/B/C` path from the root, where `..` climbs to the parent; nil when nothing matches.
docs.instantiate: Build a scene document (TOML text, not a path) under a parent; `{ scripts: false }` leaves scripts unattached.
docs.node_by_id: The node carrying a stable id, which survives the rename and the reparent a path does not; nil when nothing carries it. `under` bounds the search to one subtree, for a tool holding more than one tree.
docs.preset_info: A preset's `description`, `tags`, the `components` it adds, and `parts`: each component's own properties by name. Nil for a name nothing registered.
docs.presets: The names of every registered preset.
docs.set_variable: Write a scene variable, coerced to the type it was declared with. Every node declaring `on_variable_changed` hears about it at the end of the tick; writing the value it already holds says nothing.
docs.source: A scene file's raw TOML text, project-relative and found inside the pack in a packed run; nil when missing.
docs.switch: Replace the scene with another one at the end of this tick, so a script asking inside `update` is not freeing the tree it runs in. `fade` is seconds the renderer crosses over; reset is a switch to the same file.
docs.tagged: Every node filed under a tag, in tree order; what a scene's `tags` key and `node.add_tag` feed.
docs.variable: A scene variable's value, or nil for a name nothing declared. A scene declares them under `[variables]`.
docs.variables: Every declared variable as `{ name, type, value, persist }`, in name order.
docs.warnings: What is off about the node, as `{ component, property, message }`: a component missing one it expects, a write its component refused, and what a component says of itself. `property` is nil for the whole component; advisory only.
docs.with_component: Every node carrying the named component, in tree order. What a script asks instead of walking the tree itself.

modules.name: scene

modules.doc: Loads other scripts, inspects what they declare and calls into them; a failure stays contained.

docs.api: Every module scripts can reach, as the JSON string `balaur api` prints; a tool reads the live engine rather than a file that may be stale.
docs.attempt: Call a function, answering `(true, value)` when it returned and `(false, message)` when it failed.
docs.check: Every compiler diagnostic about the given source, as `[#{ file, line, column, severity, message }]`; an editor passes the buffer it is showing.
docs.complete: Every completion valid at that caret, as `[#{ label, kind, detail, doc, insert }]`; an editor passes the buffer it is showing.
docs.definition: Where the name at that caret is defined, as `#{ file, line, column, url }`; engine API carries its reference page rather than a file.
docs.exports: The tunable properties a script declares in `exports()`, with their defaults.
docs.find: Every place that text appears across the files this one's `mod` declarations reach, matched as text rather than as an identifier.
docs.format: That source laid out by Rune's own formatter; the source unchanged when it will not parse.
docs.functions: The public functions a script file declares, with their argument names.
docs.hover: What is under that caret, as `#{ title, detail, doc }`, or `()` when it is nothing the engine knows.
docs.references: Every place that name appears as a whole word across the files this one's `mod` declarations reach, as `[#{ file, line, column, url }]`.
docs.rename: Every file a rename would rewrite, as `[#{ file, source }]`; nothing is written, so a caller can show the list first.
docs.replace: Every file a find and replace would rewrite, as `[#{ file, source }]`; nothing is written, so a caller can show the list first.
docs.require: Load another script file as a module, compiled once and shared by every caller afterwards.
docs.shared: Wrap a script function so another script's code can call it, with whatever arguments the caller brings.
docs.signature: The call the caret is inside, as `#{ title, detail, doc, active }`, where `active` is the argument being typed.
docs.store: Keep any value under a key for as long as the app runs, held by reference: state no node owns, like a class's static variable.
docs.stored: What `store` kept under a key, the same value rather than a copy; nil when nothing was.
docs.symbols: What that file declares, as `[#{ name, kind, detail, line, column }]`: its public functions and its `exports()` properties.

signatures.complete: (path: string, source: string, line: int, column: int)
signatures.definition: (path: string, source: string, line: int, column: int)
signatures.hover: (path: string, source: string, line: int, column: int)
signatures.rename: (path: string, source: string, from: string, to: string)

modules.doc: Every setting the engine, its plugins and the game declare, by path: `physics/solver_iterations` is `[physics] solver_iterations` in `project.toml`. `define` adds your own; `[override.<platform>]` tables answer per platform.

docs.all: Every defined setting as `{ path, scope, spec }`, in definition order.
docs.base: What the file says, ignoring every override: what a settings screen edits.
docs.clear: Forget one value, so the next write drops the key: how an override is removed.
docs.define: Declare a setting of your own: `type`, `default`, and optionally `min`, `max`, `options`, `help`, `order` and `applies`. A path starting `editor/` is kept on this machine; anything else ships with the game.
docs.get: One setting's value here: the narrowest `[override.<tag>]` this platform answers to, else what was set, else what its definition defaults to, else nil.
docs.known_tags: Every tag a project may write an override for: the engine's, then the project's own from `[export] tags`.
docs.merge_toml: Read values out of a TOML text, folding them onto what is already loaded.
docs.overrides: The tags this project holds an override for at `path`, in tag order.
docs.revision: A count that moves whenever a setting is defined, set, cleared or loaded: a screen listing settings rebuilds its rows when it moves, not every frame.
docs.set: Change one setting, in memory. Whether it takes effect now or on the next run is the setting's own business; `all` reports it as `applies`.
docs.tags: The names this run answers to, broad to narrow: the kind of machine, the operating system, the architecture, the build.
docs.to_toml: The text one scope would write, starting from `existing` so anything no setting describes survives. Scope is "project" or "editor".

modules.name: settings

modules.doc: Bones under a rig node: their rest pose and the order a skin numbers joints in. A bone is any node carrying `bone2d` or `bone3d`.

docs.apply_rest: Move every bone under the node back to its rest transform.
docs.bones: The bones under the node in tree order, the order a skin numbers them in, the node itself first when it is one.
docs.overwrite_rest: Record every bone's current transform under the node as its new rest pose.

modules.name: skeleton

modules.doc: Localization: one `strings/<locale>.toml` per language, keys to strings. `[locale]` in `project.toml` sets the starting locale and the fallback; a key neither has comes back as itself.

docs.locales: Every locale the project ships a `strings/<locale>.toml` for, in name order.
docs.set_locale: Switch locale; the next `tr` answers in it, which for a widget showing a key is the next frame.
docs.set_root: Read the catalogues from this directory instead of the project root, forgetting the ones already read; an empty string puts it back. For a host running a project other than its own: the editor, whose own root has no `strings/`, so without this every `text_key` in a played scene draws as its key.
docs.system_locale: The locale the operating system reports, like `en-US`, or nil when it says nothing; recorded with the session. A game picks its starting locale from it once and saves the choice.
docs.tr: The string for a key in the current locale. `{name}` in it is replaced by the argument called `name`, and an `n` argument also picks the plural form the locale's language calls for.

modules.name: strings

modules.doc: Waiting inside an async handler: `init` and event handlers may await; `update` is synchronous.

docs.frames: Park an async handler for a number of fixed steps; counted on the tick, so a replay waits exactly as long.
docs.seconds: Park an async handler for a span of simulation time, in fixed steps; the wall clock never enters it.
docs.wait: Park an async handler until the engine wakes the token it was given.

modules.name: task

modules.doc: TOML text to and from script tables, the format of scene files, asset definitions and component properties.

docs.encode: A table written back out as TOML text; a node or callback in it is not data and is an error.
docs.parse: The table a TOML document describes; an error on text that does not parse.
docs.patch: The document's text with this table's keys written into it, keeping every comment, the key order and any table the value does not name. What a tool saving a hand-written file uses instead of `encode`.

modules.name: toml

modules.doc: Immediate-mode UI redrawn from a script's `draw_ui` every frame: panels, layout containers and widgets. HUD elements in the scene tree are the `widget` component.

docs.activate_focused: Activate the focused widget, exactly as a click on it would.
docs.add_space: Insert blank space along the current layout, in design pixels.
docs.align_right: Lay the callback's widgets out against the right edge, still declared left to right.
docs.available_height: The height left in the current container, in design pixels.
docs.available_width: The width left in the current container, in design pixels.
docs.bottom_panel: Dock a strip across the bottom of the window and draw the callback inside it; `height` is in design pixels. Answers the height it ended up with.
docs.button: Draw a button, or a row with its caption at the start when `text_align = "start"`; true on the frame it was clicked. `enabled = false` greys it out and swallows the click. `menu` hangs a right-click menu off it, `menu_click` one that opens on a left click.
docs.button_rect: Where the last `button` was drawn, as `#{ x, y, width, height }` in design pixels; empty before one has. An immediate control has no node `widget_rect` can be asked about, so a caller that wants to point at one reads it back here, straight after the call that drew it.
docs.central_panel: Draw the callback into whatever room the docked panels left over.
docs.central_rect: The x, y, width and height of the surface being drawn into, in design pixels.
docs.circle_button: Draw a round button holding one glyph, `diameter` design pixels across; true on the frame it was clicked. `enabled = false` greys it out and swallows the click.
docs.click: Click a widget node as the pointer would, at the next tick and with no window needed: what a test harness drives the game with. False for a node a pointer could not click, hidden, disabled or not a widget; `#{ hidden: true }` clicks a hidden one anyway, as a test emitting its signal would.
docs.code_editor: Draw an editable, highlighted buffer with a gutter; returns the text, whether it changed, any line clicked, and the caret as `#{ x, y, index }`.
docs.code_line: Draw one read-only code row from a list of `{ text, color, strong }` spans, with a gutter label on the left.
docs.color_picker: Draw a color picker over `value`, an `[r, g, b, a]` of unit floats; returns the colour and whether it changed.
docs.column: Lay the callback's widgets out in a column.
docs.complete_theme: The theme document with every colour and size it leaves out derived from its sources, and `dark` stated.
docs.contrast: The WCAG contrast ratio between two `#rrggbb` colours, 1 to 21. Body text wants 4.5, large or bold text 3.
docs.contrast_pairs: Every ink a `widget_theme` document's roles draw on the fill each draws it on, as `{ role, ink, fill, ratio, need }`. A role with no fill is read on the `ground` token; `need` is 3 for large or bold text and 4.5 otherwise.
docs.dialog: Draw the callback in a centered dialog over a dimming scrim; true on the frame the scrim was clicked. `width`, `height` and `top` size and place it, `fill`, `stroke` and `scrim` colour it; height follows the content when it is not given.
docs.dot: Draw a filled circle in a `#rrggbb` colour, `diameter` design pixels across.
docs.dropdown: Draw a pill-shaped select over a list of strings; returns the selection and whether it changed this frame.
docs.edit: Change a widget node's value as the reader would, at the next tick, so it announces `change`: a number for a slider or a number field, a colour for a swatch, a boolean for a fold, text for a field, a dropdown's pick, a list's row or a tab. False for a disabled widget or a value its kind does not take.
docs.fill_rows: `fill_strip` for a form: each row table is a `label`, its `controls` and an optional `draw` hatch, laid beside `label_width`, or above the controls when `stacked`. `full` spans both columns; `height`, `tooltip`, `label_role` and `slot_role` dress it.
docs.fill_strip: Put one widget node per control table under the node at `host`, made, reused and hidden as the list changes; a node is written only when its table changed. A control's `on` hears the reader's edit and `on_submit` hears Enter as they happen, so a strip that did not change need not be filled again, and a control carrying `controls` is a row holding them. True when a control's table differed from the last one written to it.
docs.finish_loading: Say the load is through, which lets a held splash go once `splash_seconds` has also passed. The editor calls it once its shell has settled.
docs.focus_next: Move focus to the next widget in scene order, wrapping past the last.
docs.focus_previous: Move focus to the previous widget in scene order, wrapping past the first.
docs.focused_widget: The widget node focus is on, or nil.
docs.frame: Wrap the callback in a box with optional `fill`, `stroke`, `corner_radius` and padding, in design pixels. `tooltip`, `menu` and `menu_click` make the whole box answer the pointer, the way a button does, and a `hover` table is what it wears while the pointer is over it.
docs.height_class: How much height this screen has, as `ui::SHORT` or `ui::TALL`.
docs.image: Draw a PNG from the project, sized by `width`/`height` in design pixels and cached by path. `region` (`[x, y, w, h]` in the image's own pixels) draws one part of it, which is how an atlas is shown a tile at a time.
docs.image_button: The same picture, answering a click: returns whether it was clicked this frame. Takes every `image` option plus `selected`, which draws the `stroke` border a chosen tile needs, and the `menu`/`menu_click` callbacks a pill takes.
docs.label: Draw a line of text; `font_size`, `font_family`, `text_color`, `font_weight`, `wrap` and `truncate` style it.
docs.layout_y: How far down the current panel the next widget will land, in design pixels: the same origin `rect_stroke` measures from.
docs.left_panel: Dock a column down the left of the window and draw the callback inside it; `width` is in design pixels. Answers the width it ended up with.
docs.list: A scroll area of `count` rows of one height, calling the callback only for the rows on screen. `row_height` is the row, in design pixels.
docs.menu_item: Draw a row inside a menu, `width` design pixels across and with `trailing` set against its right edge; true on the frame it was clicked, which also closes the menu unless `keep_open` says otherwise.
docs.number_field: Draw a number dragged sideways to change it; returns the value and whether this frame changed it.
docs.overlay: Draw the callback in a foreground area at `x`/`y` design pixels, above the panels and the widget layer. `width`/`height` fix its size, and `fill`, `stroke`, `corner_radius` and padding make it a sheet. `interactive = false` for one that is only read, which hands its clicks to what is behind it.
docs.pasted_text: The text pasted this frame, empty otherwise: the platform clipboard is not readable on demand.
docs.progress_bar: Draw how far along something is: a `track` with `part` of it filled in `fill`, `width` by `height` design pixels, cornered by `corner_radius`. `part` is 0 to 1, and one outside that is held at the nearest end.
docs.rect_stroke: Outline a rectangle at x/y/w/h design pixels from the current panel's corner, `dashed` when asked.
docs.request_repaint: Run the UI pass this frame even when lazy, and the frame itself under `[window] low_processor`; call it every frame something on screen moves without input, such as while the scene plays. `#{ after: seconds }` asks for one that far ahead instead.
docs.right_panel: Dock a column down the right of the window and draw the callback inside it; `width` is in design pixels. Answers the width it ended up with.
docs.row: Lay the callback's widgets out in a row; `width`, `height` and `tight` size it, in design pixels.
docs.scale: The global UI scale: how many screen pixels a design pixel is drawn at, on top of the display's own.
docs.scroll: Put the callback in a scroll area. `axis` is `vertical` (the default), `horizontal` or `both`; `max_height` and `max_width` cap it, `stick_to_end` follows new content, and `scroll_offset` scrolls it to that many design pixels along, one number along `axis` or `[across, down]`, below zero leaving an axis where it is.
docs.separator: Draw a one-pixel rule across the container, in the given `#rrggbb` colour when one is passed.
docs.set_clipboard: Copy text to the system clipboard.
docs.set_field_text: Overwrite what the field with this `id` is editing, leaving the seed its `value` option last wrote alone.
docs.set_focus: Put focus on a widget node. A node focus cannot activate is refused at the next draw.
docs.set_keyboard_navigation: Let the arrows, Tab, Enter and Space move and activate the focused widget. Off unless asked for, so a game that moves with the arrows does not click its own HUD; `standard_app` turns it on for a project declaring the `ui_*` actions.
docs.set_lazy: Run the UI pass only when something asks for it (input, `request_repaint`, a log line, an asset reload, an egui animation, or the idle tick every 250 ms, which waits out a drag the UI is no part of) and re-present the last pass in between. Off by default: a HUD that reads live state each frame should leave it off. Ignored offscreen.
docs.set_load_progress: Report how far a load is, zero to one. This is what holds `[application] splash` past its seconds, and what draws the bar under it.
docs.set_scale: Set the global UI scale, clamped to between 0.25 and 3.0. It is egui's zoom factor, so it grows every control and every font; `screen_size` already answers in the design pixels it leaves.
docs.set_theme: Dress every `ui::*` call from a theme document, the shape a `widget_theme` file holds: source colours under `colors`, sizes under `sizes`, and a `roles` table of named looks a call takes with `role`. What the document leaves out is derived from its sources.
docs.set_widget_layer: Turn drawing of the scene's `widget` nodes on or off, and confine it to an x/y/w/h rect in design pixels.
docs.set_widget_surface: The same for one named surface: roots whose `layer` is this name draw here instead. A name nothing has set takes the default surface.
docs.shortcut: Whether this chord was pressed this frame, consuming it: modifiers and a key joined by `+`, as in `"cmd+shift+s"` or `"f5"`. `cmd` is the platform's command key, Command on a Mac and Control everywhere else.
docs.slider: Draw a horizontal slider between `min` and `max`; returns the value after this frame and whether it moved.
docs.spacing: Set the gap between the current container's widgets, in design pixels.
docs.switch: Draw an on/off switch; returns the state after this frame and whether it was clicked.
docs.tab_rect: Where a `tabs` page's own button in the strip was last drawn, as `#{ x, y, width, height }` in design pixels; empty before the strip has drawn. `widget_rect` on the same node answers with the page body.
docs.takes_pointer_at: Whether the UI would take a press at this point, in design pixels, by the same layers as `wants_pointer`: what an editor asks of a point it is about to act on.
docs.text_field: Draw a single-line text box keyed by `id`; returns its text, whether it changed, and whether Enter was pressed.
docs.top_panel: Dock a strip across the top of the window and draw the callback inside it; `height` is in design pixels. Answers the height it ended up with.
docs.wants_keyboard: Whether a UI widget holds keyboard focus, so the game should leave this frame's key presses alone.
docs.wants_pointer: Whether the UI has the pointer or finger, so the game should leave it alone: what stops a tap on a HUD button also firing the shot behind it. A press is routed once, from the top: an open dialog, then a popup or window, then a widget that is not `interactive = false` or a seam between boxes, and the world last; it keeps that answer until the button comes up. Answers outside `draw_ui` too; false without a window.
docs.widget_rect: Where a `widget` node was last drawn, as `#{ x, y, width, height }` in design pixels; empty until it has drawn once.
docs.width_class: How much width this screen has, as `ui::NARROW`, `ui::MEDIUM` or `ui::WIDE`. Read every frame: a rotation changes it. A run with no window answers `ui::WIDE`.
docs.window: Draw the callback in a floating window the user drags and resizes; false once its close button is used. `resizable`, `movable` and `closable` are on unless turned off, `collapsible` and `constrain` off unless turned on; `header = false` drops the title bar, `default_open = false` starts it folded, and `min_width`, `min_height`, `max_width` and `max_height` bound its size, as the `window` widget's keys of those names do.
docs.window_size: The window's width and height, in design pixels; a headless run answers the `[window]` size the project states.

modules.name: ui

modules.doc: A long-lived socket for text or binary frames. Events reach the node's `on_websocket_event` (or `on_event`) as a map with `socket` and `kind`: `open`, `message`, `binary`, `closed` or `error`, each an `EVENT_*` constant. An `error` carries its `reason`, and the HTTP `status` when a server refused the upgrade.

docs.close: Ask the connection to close, which still delivers a `closed` event with its `code`; false when it was already gone.
docs.connect: Open a connection and return the id `send` and `close` take, which `task.wait` resumes on with the `open` or `error` event; options are `on_event`, `compression` and `headers`.
docs.send: Queue a frame on the connection, text for a string and binary for bytes; false when it is already gone.
docs.state: Where the connection is: `connecting`, `open`, `closing` or `closed`, each a `STATE_*` constant.

modules.doc: The OS window and the display under it: mode, cursor, app icon, keep-awake, the safe area and the refresh rate.

docs.refresh_rate: Frames per second the display refreshes at, as measured over the last frames; 60 with no window.
docs.safe_area: The display's insets in pixels, `{ left, top, right, bottom }`: what a notch or a home bar covers, read once per frame and recorded. Zero on a desktop.
docs.set_app_icon: Set the application icon, the dock or taskbar one, from a PNG or an SVG in the project. `opts.plate` colours the disc a macOS dock icon sits on, white by default. Replaces `[application] icon` for the run.
docs.set_cursor_grab: Confine the cursor to the window, for FPS-style mouse look.
docs.set_cursor_hidden: Hide or show the mouse cursor over the window.
docs.set_fullscreen: Put the window into borderless fullscreen on the current monitor, or back into a window.
docs.set_keep_awake: Keep the screen from dimming while the game runs: a page takes a wake lock, a phone its equivalent, a desktop needs nothing.
docs.set_window_mode: `windowed`, `maximized`, `fullscreen` (borderless) or `exclusive` (the monitor's largest video mode): the same choice as `[window] mode`.
